summary: Re-run the 5 failed Christmas Chaos reviewers (playtest, visual, server code, client code, game design) with retries

result.summary:
I played the game end to end. One host socket, one TV socket and six player sockets (three teams) drove 96 spins over 5 games, and every wheel segment came up: hotseat 13, popculture 15, dare 14, christmas 24, doubledown 8, allplay 5, sounditout 7, steal 9. A Playwright pass in headless Edge checked what the real host, TV and phone pages showed. The spin-timeout races were run against the unmodified 5.5s timer, on PORT=4101. The server is stopped and the port is free. No project files were changed.

What works:
- One spin per turn: a double-tapped SPIN (40ms apart) gives exactly one spin, and the result arrives after 5506ms. A teammate tapping SPIN at the same moment as the host button also gives exactly one spin.
- Players on other teams cannot spin.
- Three players buzzing at once gives exactly one winner.
- Hot seat runs through all its questions correctly.
- Rounds advance correctly, and the game-end standings are sorted correctly.
- The TV wheel stops on the segment the server picked.
- There were no JavaScript errors on any page.
- A refreshed phone can re-join and spin.

What fails: answers to your questions:
- **Phone screen-lock / reconnect:** the player is silently dropped. Their phone still shows "It's YOUR team's turn!" and the SPIN button, but taps and buzzes are ignored.
- **Page refresh:** works, but the player lands back on the join screen with an empty name and has to re-join by hand.
- **Host removes a team:** phones on later teams keep the old team number for the whole game. The wrong phones get the SPIN button, and the team whose turn it is gets none.
- **Host-only events from a player socket:** nothing stops them.
- **Reset during the 5.5s spin:** the pending spin result still lands in the new game. A Full Reset done this way leaves the lobby locked.
- **"Play Again":** it disconnects every player behind the scenes, but every phone still shows "You're in!".
- **Server crashes:** a missing payload, or a steal from a team that doesn't exist, kills the server and all the scores.

Gameplay bugs:
- **Sound It Out:** the TV shows the song title to the whole room.
- **Plain trivia:** any team can buzz in, so ALL PLAY is identical to it.
- **Buzzer:** a player who answered wrong is not locked out when it reopens.
- **Double Down:** never appears on the TV, carries over to the next team, and is used up by penalties or by points given to another team.
- **Steal:** gives the full 100 even when the victim has less, and works again if the host clicks twice.

The scripts and logs are in C:/Users/mleys/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d489c8c283eb5306/1f6a997f-d385-4b62-994e-3617bc11ff4c/scratchpad/review/playtest/: play2.js (output in run2.txt), pw2.js (pw2.txt), realtime.js (realtime.txt), crash.js (crash.txt), xss.js, and the screenshots in shots/. Two of those TV screenshots (P6 and P9) show a "BUZZ IN NOW!" box that my test script caused by restarting the game mid-play. It is not a bug and is not in the findings.

findings.title: Phone screen-lock/reconnect turns the player into a ghost: SPIN and BUZZ are silently ignored
findings.detail: Players are keyed by socket.id, and disconnect deletes them (server.js:356). When a phone locks and wakes, socket.io reconnects with a NEW id, but player.html never sends join-game again: hasJoined/myTeamIndex live only in memory, and there is no 'connect' handler. The phone still shows the game. Repro (play2.js RC1-4): Alice on active team 0; alice.s.io.engine.close(); auto-reconnect old=qGpJ... new=7wIQ...; server players = Bob,Carol,Dave,Erin,Frank. Alice spin-wheel -> 0 spin-start (rejected at server.js:221). On an open buzzer, buzzer-press -> 0 buzzer-winner (server.js:245). Real page (pw2.js P2): after the reconnect Bob's phone shows '🎄 It's YOUR team's turn!' and the SPIN button. The tap does nothing, and the button stays disabled (shots/P2-bob-after-reconnect-dead-spin.png). Refresh (P3) is a related problem: the phone goes back to the join screen with an empty name, and the player must re-join by hand. At a party, phones lock constantly.
findings.fix: Give each phone a stable id. In player.html: `let pid = localStorage.getItem('ccPid') || Math.random().toString(36).slice(2); localStorage.setItem('ccPid', pid);`. On join, save {name, teamIndex} to localStorage too. Add `socket.on('connect', () => { const s = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('ccMe')||'null'); if (s) socket.emit('join-game', { ...s, pid }); })`. On page load, skip the join screen if ccMe exists. (crypto.randomUUID is not available over plain-http LAN.) In server.js, key players by pid: `state.players[pid] = { id: pid, name, teamIndex, connected: true }; socket.data.pid = pid;`. Look up `state.players[socket.data.pid]` in spin-wheel and buzzer-press. On disconnect set `connected = false` instead of deleting the player.

findings.title: 'Play Again (keep teams)' disconnects every player; phones still say "You're in!" but can't spin or buzz
findings.detail: reset-game calls makeState(), which empties state.players. Every phone still has hasJoined=true, so it shows the waiting screen as if it were joined. Repro (play2.js RS1/RS2): after a game, reset-game leaves players=0. start-game, then a team-0 phone sends spin-wheel -> 0 spin-start. Real page (pw2.js P4): after Play Again, Bob sees "You're in!". After Start, his SPIN button is visible, and tapping it gives 0 spin-starts (shots/P4-bob-after-play-again.png). Buzzers are dead for everyone too, so trivia can't be played until every guest refreshes and re-joins.
findings.fix: In reset-game keep the roster: `const savedPlayers = state.players; state = makeState(); state.teams = savedTeams; state.players = savedPlayers; state.totalRounds = ...`. Also cancel any pending spin timer (see the spin-timer finding).

findings.title: Removing a team in the lobby desyncs every later team's phone for the whole game
findings.detail: The server re-indexes players (p.teamIndex--). But player.html caches myTeamIndex at join (line 393) and never re-reads it from state.players. Repro (pw2.js P1): teams Elves/Reindeer/Snowmen/Angels; Alice->Elves, Bob->Reindeer, Carol->Snowmen; host removes Elves. Phone badges then read Alice='Reindeer', Bob='Snowmen', Carol='Angels', but the server has Bob=Reindeer, Carol=Snowmen, and Alice removed. On Reindeer's turn, Alice (no longer a player) sees "It's YOUR team's turn!" and the SPIN button, and her tap gives 0 spins. Bob, who really is on the active team, sees "Reindeer's turn" and no SPIN button (shots/P1-*.png). The '(you)' marker and buzz toasts are wrong as well. The server also accepts join-game for a team that doesn't exist (play2.js L4: teamIndex 9 accepted). Removing a typo team after people have joined is a likely thing for a host to do.
findings.fix: In player.html state-update: `const me = state.players.find(p => p.id === pid /* or socket.id */); if (hasJoined && !me) { hasJoined = false; show('join-screen'); hide('game-screen'); hide('waiting-screen'); toast('Your team was removed, please re-join'); return; } if (me) myTeamIndex = me.teamIndex;`. In server join-game: `if (!state.teams[teamIndex] || typeof name !== 'string' || !name.trim()) return;`.

findings.title: Sound It Out shows the song title on the TV for the whole room, and on every phone of the guessing team
findings.detail: tv.html renders `🎵 ${songTitle} — ${artist}` in #sound-title as soon as the challenge arrives. player.html shows the title to everyone on the active team (isMyTurn), and that is the team meant to guess the hummed song. Repro (pw2.js P6): spin until sounditout. TV #sound-title is visible: '🎵 All I Want for Christmas Is You — Mariah Carey'. Teammate Alice's phone shows 'Hum or whistle: "All I Want for Christmas Is You" by Mariah Carey' (shots/P6-tv-sounditout-song-visible.png). The segment is pointless every time it lands (1 in 12 spins).
findings.fix: In tv.html showChallenge: show sound-title only `if (state.answerRevealed)`. In the server, send the song only to the hummer: record the spinner's socket id in spin-wheel (for host-spin, pick a random player on the active team), then call `io.to(hummerId).emit('secret-song', { songTitle, artist })` in processSegment. Strip songTitle/artist/answer from publicState until answerRevealed. player.html shows the title only on 'secret-song'.

findings.title: Any connected phone can crash the server and wipe all scores (malformed payload or bad steal index)
findings.detail: Every handler destructures its payload with no default, and steal-execute has no bounds check. Verified with crash.js against the unmodified server: steal-execute {fromTeamIndex:7,toTeamIndex:0} -> 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading score)' at server.js:275, and the process exits. award-points, join-game, create-team and steal-execute sent with no payload -> 'Cannot destructure property ... of undefined', and the process dies each time. All game state is in memory, so the scores are lost. Nothing reachable from the normal UI sends these, but there is no auth (see the next finding), so any curious guest with devtools can.
findings.fix: Default every destructure, e.g. `socket.on('steal-execute', ({ fromTeamIndex, toTeamIndex } = {}) => { if (!state.teams[fromTeamIndex] || !state.teams[toTeamIndex]) return; ... })`, and the same for all handlers. Add a last-resort guard: `process.on('uncaughtException', e => console.error('handler error', e));`.

findings.title: No host authorization: a player socket can award points, change turns, restart or reset the game
findings.detail: Repro (play2.js AU1), all sent from player Erin's socket mid-game, all accepted: award-points {teamIndex:2, points:5000} (team2 0->5000); override-score; steal-execute with no steal segment (team2 -> 5100); next-turn (turn moved to team 1); host-spin (a spin happened); start-game (round reset to 1, scores kept); reset-game (phase lobby, all players dropped). host.html is just another socket.io client.
findings.fix: Have host.html connect with `io({ auth: { hostKey: new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('key') } })`. The server generates a key at startup and prints `http://IP:PORT/host?key=XXXX`. In `io.on('connection')`, set `socket.data.isHost = socket.handshake.auth?.hostKey === HOST_KEY`, then wrap host handlers: `const hostOnly = fn => (...a) => { if (socket.data.isHost) fn(...a); };` and use `socket.on('award-points', hostOnly(...))` for create/remove-team, set-rounds, start-game, host-spin, reveal, award, steal, hotseat-next, open/close-buzzer, next-turn, override-score, reset-game and full-reset.

findings.title: Reset Scores / Full Reset during the 5.5s spin: the old spin result lands in the new game; Full Reset leaves the lobby locked
findings.detail: The spin setTimeout is never cancelled, and processSegment doesn't check the phase. Repro (realtime.js, unmodified 5.5s timer). R3: Alice spins; 2s later host Reset Scores -> phase=lobby; 3.7s later phase=challenge with a trivia question showing, players=0; host create-team 'Late' is rejected (teams stay Elves,Reindeer) because create-team needs phase==='lobby'. R4: Alice spins; host Full Reset -> lobby; after the timer phase=challenge with 0 teams; create-team x2 -> teams=0, phase=challenge. The host can't set up a new game until they press Full Reset a second time, and the host page shows the in-game panel with no teams.
findings.fix: Add `let spinToken = 0;` and, in spin-wheel/host-spin: `const tok = ++spinToken; setTimeout(() => { if (tok === spinToken && state.phase === 'spinning') processSegment(seg); }, 5500);`. Increment spinToken in reset-game, full-reset and next-turn.

findings.title: Next Turn pressed while the wheel spins: the old spin result hijacks the next team's turn
findings.detail: next-turn has no phase guard, and the Next Turn button is always enabled. Repro (realtime.js R2): Alice spins; 1.5s later host Next Turn -> playing, team 1. 5.5s later phase=challenge, currentSegment=null (cleared by next-turn), currentChallenge set to a question, buzzerOpen=true. Bob (now active) sends spin-wheel -> 0 spin-starts. Because currentSegment is null, the host page shows 'Waiting for spin…' with Spin disabled (host.html:607, 688). Phones hide the challenge and buzzer (player.html:465, 474). The TV shows 'Waiting for next spin…' plus 'BUZZ IN NOW!'. The host has to press Next Turn again, which skips Bob's team.
findings.fix: In next-turn: `if (['lobby','spinning','gameend'].includes(state.phase)) return;`. Also apply the spinToken fix from the previous finding. In host.html state-update, disable the Next Turn button while state.phase === 'spinning'.

findings.title: Plain Christmas/Pop Culture trivia opens the buzzer to every team, so ALL PLAY is the same as normal trivia
findings.detail: processSegment handles 'trivia' and 'allplay' identically (buzzerOpen=true for everyone), and buzzer-press never checks the team. Repro (play2.js B2): Pop Culture on team 2's turn; Alice (team 0), a team-1 player and a team-2 player buzz together -> the winner is Alice from team 0. The active team's question was stolen. B5: ALL PLAY differs only in points (150 vs 100). Seven of the 12 wheel segments are effectively free-for-all buzzer races, which defeats the 'your turn' structure.
findings.fix: Choose one model. Option (a): for type 'trivia', set `state.buzzerOpen = false` and let the active team answer aloud, keeping the buzzer for 'allplay' only. Option (b): in buzzer-press add `if (state.currentSegment?.type === 'trivia' && player.teamIndex !== state.currentTeamIndex) return;`, and change player.html:465 to show the buzzer for trivia only when isMyTurn.

findings.title: No lockout: after a wrong answer and Open Buzzer, the same (fastest) player wins the buzzer again
findings.detail: open-buzzer clears buzzerWinner without remembering who already answered, and player.html re-enables every buzzer button. Repro (play2.js B3): Alice wins the buzz; host presses Open Buzzer; Alice buzzes again -> buzzer-winner = Alice. In a real race, the person who just answered wrong is always fastest to re-buzz.
findings.fix: Add `state.buzzLocked = []` to makeState and reset it in processSegment. In open-buzzer: `if (state.buzzerWinner) state.buzzLocked.push(state.buzzerWinner.playerId)` (or lock the whole teamIndex). In buzzer-press: `if (state.buzzLocked.includes(socket.id)) return;`. Include buzzLocked in publicState so player.html keeps that phone's button disabled.

findings.title: Double Down never appears on the TV; the dedicated 'Double Down!' texts are dead code
findings.detail: The CSS says `#double-down-banner { display:none }` and shows it only with `.show`. The JS only removes the `hidden` class, so the banner can never be visible. The server sets currentChallenge=null for doubledown, and the host, player and TV branches that print 'Double Down! Spin again…' all require currentChallenge, so they never run. Repro (pw2.js P9): wheel lands on Double Down; TV label '', TV text 'Spin the wheel!', banner computed display:none; host shows 'Waiting for spin…'. Only the phone pill and the host banner show anything (shots/P9-tv-doubledown.png).
findings.fix: In tv.html:503-505 use `ddb.classList.toggle('show', state.doubleDownActive)` (or delete `display:none` from #double-down-banner). In server.js:162 set `state.currentChallenge = { type: 'doubledown' }` so the existing host/player/TV doubledown branches render, or render those branches from the segment alone.

findings.title: Double Down logic: carries over to the next team, and is used up by penalties or by points to another team
findings.detail: Repro (play2.js). D2: Double Down lands, host presses Next Turn -> doubleDownActive is still true on team 2's turn. D3: while it's active, host gives a wrong-answer -50 to another team -> that team loses 100 and the double is used up. D4: on an open-buzzer question another team wins and gets 100 -> they receive 200 and the active team's double is gone. Only a positive award to the active team (D5) behaves as the wheel text says.
findings.fix: Add `state.doubleDownTeam` (set it to currentTeamIndex when Double Down lands). In award-points: `if (state.doubleDownActive && pts > 0 && teamIndex === state.doubleDownTeam) { pts *= 2; state.doubleDownActive = false; }`. In next-turn: `state.doubleDownActive = false;`.

findings.title: Steal gives the full 100 even when the victim has less, and works again on a second click
findings.detail: Repro (play2.js ST1): victim at 30 -> 0 (lost 30), thief +100. ST2: steal clicked twice -> victim 500->300, thief +200. The steal panel stays on screen after a steal, which invites a second click. The server never checks that the current segment is a steal (AU1: steal-execute accepted during a non-steal turn).
findings.fix: `if (state.currentSegment?.effect !== 'steal' || state.stealDone) return; const from = state.teams[fromTeamIndex], to = state.teams[toTeamIndex]; if (!from || !to || from === to) return; const amt = Math.min(100, from.score); from.score -= amt; to.score += amt; state.stealDone = true;`. Reset stealDone in processSegment and include it in publicState so host.html hides the steal panel once done.

findings.title: Reveal Answer leaves the buzzer open: players can buzz after the answer is on the TV
findings.detail: Repro (play2.js B4 / pw2.js P11): with the buzzer open and no winner, host clicks Reveal. TV shows '✓ Todd Chester…' and still 'BUZZ IN NOW!'. Carol's phone buzzer is still visible, and her buzz is accepted and announced (shots/P11-carol-can-buzz-after-reveal.png).
findings.fix: In reveal-answer add `state.buzzerOpen = false;`.

findings.title: TV refreshed or reconnected at game end shows 'Game Over!' with no standings
findings.detail: #end-results is filled only by the one-time 'game-end' event. The state-update gameend branch only toggles screens. Repro (play2.js E3, pw2.js P5): before reload, end-results = '🥇 Reindeer — 300 pts … 🥈 Elves — 0 pts'. After tv.reload() it is empty (shots/P5-tv-refresh-at-gameend.png). Smart-TV browsers reload or sleep often, and this is the finale.
findings.fix: In tv.html's gameend state-update branch, render end-results from `[...state.teams].sort((a,b) => b.score - a.score)`, the same template as the game-end handler.

findings.title: Extra Next Turn after game end restarts play at 'Round 3 of 2'
findings.detail: Repro (play2.js E4): 2 rounds x 3 teams, 6x next-turn -> gameend; one more next-turn (e.g. a double-click on the last Next Turn over slow Wi-Fi) -> phase=playing, round 3/2, team 0. The end screens disappear on every device.
findings.fix: Add `if (state.phase === 'gameend' || state.phase === 'lobby') return;` at the top of next-turn. This can share a guard with the spinning check.

findings.title: Open Buzzer during Sound It Out / Dare / Hot Seat: the TV says 'BUZZ IN NOW!' but no phone shows a buzzer
findings.detail: The host's Open Buzzer button is always available. The TV shows the prompt whenever buzzerOpen is true, but phones show the button only for trivia/allplay, and the server still accepts a buzz. Repro (play2.js SO2 / pw2.js P8): Sound It Out, Open Buzzer -> TV '🔔 BUZZ IN NOW!' visible, Carol's #buzzer-wrap hidden, yet a direct buzzer-press from her socket wins (shots/P8-*.png).
findings.fix: Pick one rule and use it everywhere. Either reject open-buzzer unless `['trivia','allplay'].includes(state.currentSegment?.type)`, or drop the segment-type check at player.html:465 so the phone follows state.buzzerOpen.

findings.title: After the last Hot Seat question the TV keeps showing it as current ('Question 5 of 5')
findings.detail: hotseat-complete sets phase='challenge' and currentChallenge=null. tv.html's state-update has no branch for that state and doesn't listen for 'hotseat-complete'. Repro (play2.js HS2 / pw2.js P10): after 5x Next Q, the TV still reads 'In which country is KFC a popular Christmas tradition?' with 'Question 5 of 5', while the host shows 'Waiting for spin…' and phones hide the challenge.
findings.fix: In tv.html add `socket.on('hotseat-complete', () => { setText('challenge-text', '🔥 Hot Seat complete!'); hide('hotseat-progress'); })`, and in state-update handle `!state.currentChallenge && state.phase === 'challenge'`.

findings.title: Host-chosen round count is silently overwritten when a team is added or removed
findings.detail: Repro (play2.js L2): host sets 2 rounds, adds a team -> totalRounds=3; sets 2 again, removes a team -> 4. A late-arriving family branch resets the host's game length without warning.
findings.fix: Set `state.roundsManual = true` in set-rounds. In create-team and remove-team, recompute only `if (!state.roundsManual)`.

findings.title: Player and team names are injected as HTML (a player name runs markup on the host page)
findings.detail: Names go into innerHTML unescaped, and maxlength=20 is enforced only in the browser. Repro (xss.js): join-game with name 'Mallory', start the game, open /host -> document.getElementById('pwn') exists. A guest can inject markup or script into the host's game-master page.
findings.fix: Add `const esc = s => String(s).replace(/[&<>"']/g, c => ({'&':'&','<':'<','>':'>','"':'"',"'":'''}[c]));` and wrap every `${t.name}` / `${p.name}` in esc(). On the server, also `name = String(name).trim().slice(0, 20)`.

findings.title: Every phone receives the answer (and song title) in state-update before Reveal
findings.detail: publicState sends the full currentChallenge, including answer/songTitle, to all sockets. Repro (play2.js A1): in 64 of 64 question spins, an other-team phone's state already held currentChallenge.answer before reveal. Only visible with devtools, so low risk at a family party.
findings.fix: `currentChallenge: state.answerRevealed || !state.currentChallenge ? state.currentChallenge : (({ answer, songTitle, artist, ...rest }) => rest)(state.currentChallenge)`. Send the full object to the host only (requires the host-key fix).

findings.title: Non-numeric points or rounds corrupt state (score becomes NaN / null, the game never ends)
findings.detail: Repro (play2.js V1): award-points {points:'abc'} -> team0.score = NaN (sent as null; boards show 'null' and it stays NaN after later awards). set-rounds {rounds:'x'} -> totalRounds NaN, so `round > totalRounds` is never true and the game cannot end. The normal UI can't send these; a player socket can (no auth).
findings.fix: In award-points: `const pts = Number(points); if (!Number.isFinite(pts)) return;`. In set-rounds: `const r = parseInt(rounds, 10); if (!Number.isInteger(r)) return;`. Do the same for override-score.

findings.title: Host toast shows '+-50 pts' for penalties and the un-doubled amount during Double Down
findings.detail: Repro (pw2.js P12/P13): clicking −50 shows '+-50 pts → Elves'. With Double Down active, clicking +150 shows '+150 pts → Reindeer' while the server added 300.
findings.fix: `const shown = gameState.doubleDownActive && points > 0 ? points * 2 : points; toast(`${shown > 0 ? '+' : ''}${shown} pts → ${gameState.teams[teamIndex]?.name}`);`

findings.title: Typed answers from phones are not implemented (buzzer only)
findings.detail: The brief says players 'use a buzzer or type answers'. player.html has no answer input (only #name-input), and the server has no answer-submit event, so answers are all spoken aloud after a buzz. Since the brief says 'or', this is acceptable, but it's worth knowing for ALL PLAY rounds, where a typed answer from every team would be fairer than a buzz race.
findings.fix: Optional. Add a text input shown during allplay, emit 'submit-answer' {text}, store it per team in state, and list the submissions on the host page with Award buttons.

result.summary:
I audited the real screens in headless Edge: host at 1440x900, TV at 1920x1080, three phones at 390x844, plus a 360x640 phone and the host page on a phone. Server ran on PORT=4102 and is now stopped. I played a full 5-team session through every state: lobby, my-turn, spinning, trivia buzzer open / won / revealed, ALL PLAY, dare, sound-it-out, hot seat, steal, double down, game end. Edge cases tested: 8 teams with 24-character names, 0 players, a phone reconnecting, Play Again, and Google Fonts blocked or stalled. I also measured font sizes, tap targets and WCAG contrast.

All screenshots and scripts are in C:/Users/mleys/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d489c8c283eb5306/1f6a997f-d385-4b62-994e-3617bc11ff4c/scratchpad/review/visual/. The earlier attempt's shots were reused because the code hasn't changed since. Its old 16-dare-* and 17-sounditout-* files were captured in the wrong state by a timing bug in that script; ignore them and use the new N-dare-* and N-sounditout-* files.

The four problems that would wreck the party:
1. The TV game-over screen is completely blank, so the finale shows nothing.
2. Sound It Out prints the song title in the biggest gold text on the TV, so the round is spoiled for everyone.
3. Any phone that locks or blips Wi-Fi is silently dropped from the game. Play Again drops every player. The dropped phones keep showing buttons that do nothing.
4. Nobody is told the real join address: the TV and host page say only "/player", with no IP and no QR code.

Beyond those, the TV is built like a laptop page rather than a 10-foot screen: text is 15–21px, the wheel is 380px (35% of the screen height), and wheel labels are about 9.5px with half of them upside down. The host cannot see the answer before revealing it. Pressing Next Turn during a spin locks the next team out of their turn. Several TV states are stale or never appear: the old answer lingers, the Hot Seat's last question stays up, and the Double Down banner never shows. Buzzing in has no impact on the TV or the phone. Two of your stated requirements aren't there: typing answers, and the timers and team votes that most dares rely on.

Colour contrast is mostly fine. The failures are team colours used as name text (1.6–3.8:1) and the white label on the gold ALL PLAY wedge (2.6:1).

findings.title: TV game-over screen is blank, so the finale shows nothing
findings.detail: tv.html:180-186 sets `#end-screen{display:none}`, and the div (tv.html:290) has no `hidden` class. show('end-screen') (tv.html:397, called at 522 and 574) only removes `.hidden`, so the element stays hidden. Measured at game end: getComputedStyle(#end-screen).display === 'none' while #end-results holds 8 rows. The TV shows an empty navy screen, and the header is stale ('Naughty List's turn | Round 3 of 3') because tv.html:496 skips header updates during gameend. Reloading the TV doesn't help. Screenshots: C:/Users/mleys/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d489c8c283eb5306/1f6a997f-d385-4b62-994e-3617bc11ff4c/scratchpad/review/visual/40-gameend-tv.png and .../visual/41-gameend-tv-after-reload.png
findings.fix: Change the CSS to `#end-screen{display:flex;...}` and add class="hidden" to <div id="end-screen">, so show() and hide() work. In the gameend branch of state-update, set round-label to 'Final Scores' and clear turn-banner. Then add a winner hero (see the end-screen design finding).

findings.title: Sound It Out shows the song title and artist on the TV as soon as the wheel lands
findings.detail: tv.html:444-445 renders `🎵 ${songTitle} — ${artist}` in .sound-title (1.8rem, weight 900, gold: the largest, brightest text on screen) the moment the challenge appears. Every guesser in the room reads 'Last Christmas — Wham!' before anyone hums. Screenshot: C:/Users/mleys/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d489c8c283eb5306/1f6a997f-d385-4b62-994e-3617bc11ff4c/scratchpad/review/visual/N-sounditout-tv.png

findings.title: A phone that locks, reconnects or refreshes is silently dropped, and its buttons then do nothing

On the phone, show a 'Reconnecting…' banner and disable buttons on 'disconnect'. result.summary:
I reviewed server.js line by line without changing any project files, then tested it. Socket clients and headless Edge ran against a test server on PORT 47613, and a crash/restart script started its own server on 47614. Both servers have been stopped. Scripts and outputs are in C:/Users/mleys/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d489c8c283eb5306/1f6a997f-d385-4b62-994e-3617bc11ff4c/scratchpad/review/server-js/ (t_state.out, t_crash.out, t_reconnect.out, t_more.out, reconnect_ghost.png).

Four problems could break the party:
1. Any malformed socket payload crashes the Node process. I reproduced this with 8 of 8 handlers. All game state is held only in memory, so a crash loses everything. I also confirmed that a restart mid-game goes back to an empty lobby.
2. A player is identified only by socket.id and is deleted on disconnect, and the phone never joins again. After a Wi-Fi drop or screen lock the phone still shows SPIN and the buzzer, but the server silently ignores both. I reproduced this in Edge.
3. "Play Again" (reset-game) and full-reset wipe every player, so every phone stops working in game 2.
4. There is no host check at all, and '/' redirects to /host. A guest who types the bare IP gets the game-master panel. I confirmed that a player socket can set any score and run full-reset.

Confirmed state-machine and timer problems:
- The 5.5s spin timer is never cancelled. A reset during a spin locks the lobby, because a team can no longer be created. Pressing Next Turn during a spin applies the old result to the next team.
- next-turn has no phase check and no duplicate guard. A double-tap skips a team, it starts the game from the lobby, it restarts a finished game, and with zero teams the current team index becomes NaN.
- Teams are referenced by index. A double-tap on remove-team deletes two teams, and phones that already joined end up with the wrong team.
- Regular trivia opens the buzzer to every team, so it plays exactly like ALL PLAY.
- Double Down goes to whichever team is awarded points next, including penalties and other teams, and it carries over past Next Turn.
- Steal can be repeated, creates points the victim did not have, and lets a team steal from itself.
- Every question's answer is sent to every connected client before the reveal.
- There is no server path at all for typing answers, which the requirements ask for.

Network: the server prints every non-internal IPv4 address in OS order. An earlier run today printed a VPN address (10.200.101.14) before the Wi-Fi address, and neither the TV nor the host page shows the real join URL. The Wi-Fi profile on this machine is Public, the firewall is on, and I found no inbound rule for node.exe. I could not test whether that blocks phones, because it needs a real phone.

Each finding below gives the file:line, the scenario I reproduced and the exact fix.

findings.title: Any malformed socket payload crashes the whole server, and all game state is lost
findings.detail: Socket.io v4 calls listeners from inside process.nextTick, so an exception in a handler is uncaught and the process exits with code 1. Reproduced 8 of 8 (t_crash.out): steal-execute {} and {fromTeamIndex:7} give 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading score)' at server.js:275. join-game, create-team, award-points, set-rounds and remove-team with no payload, and override-score with null, give 'Cannot destructure property ... of undefined' at server.js:178,183,191,203,265,336. State lives only in `let state` (server.js:57), so one bad emit, or a future bug in any handler, ends the party.
findings.fix: Add a wrapper: `const on = (ev, fn) => socket.on(ev, (p = {}, ...r) => { try { fn(p && typeof p === 'object' ? p : {}, ...r); } catch (e) { console.error(ev, e); } });` and register every handler through it. Validate every index with `const validTeam = i => Number.isInteger(i) && i >= 0 && i < state.teams.length;`. As a last resort add `process.on('uncaughtException', e => console.error('uncaught', e));`. Pair this with persistence (see the restart finding).

findings.title: Players are keyed by socket.id and deleted on disconnect; phones never rejoin, so spin and buzz are silently ignored
findings.detail: server.js:179 stores the player under socket.id and server.js:356 deletes it on disconnect. socket.io auto-reconnects with a new id, but player.html only emits join-game once (player.html:396, hasJoined stays true). Reproduced in headless Edge (t_reconnect.out): after a transport drop the id changed (BI8y...→Gb8-...), the server player list became [], the phone still showed the SPIN button, and tapping it left phase 'playing'. spin-wheel (server.js:220-221) and buzzer-press (server.js:244-245) return without telling the phone. Phone screen locks and Wi-Fi blips are constant at a party.
findings.fix: Give each player a persistent id. The client creates `playerId = localStorage.ccId ||= crypto.randomUUID()` and connects with `io({ auth: { playerId } })`. The server keys `state.players[playerId] = { id: playerId, socketId, name, teamId, connected }`. In 'connection', look up `socket.handshake.auth.playerId`. If the player exists, set socketId and connected:true, then `socket.emit('you', player)`. On disconnect set `connected = false` instead of deleting. spin-wheel and buzzer-press find the player by `socket.data.playerId`. When the server cannot find the player, emit `socket.emit('need-join')` so the phone returns to the join screen instead of failing silently.

findings.title: 'Play Again' (reset-game) and full-reset drop every joined player; all phones stop working in game 2
findings.detail: server.js:343-345 rebuilds state with makeState(), keeping teams but resetting players to {}. full-reset (server.js:351) does the same. No message tells phones to rejoin, and they keep hasJoined=true. Reproduced (t_more.out M1): Alice@0 → players [] after reset-game. After start-game, Alice tapped spin on her own team's turn and the phase stayed 'playing'. host.html:394 'Play Again (keep teams)' is the obvious end-of-game button.
findings.fix: In reset-game keep the players: `const savedPlayers = state.players; state = makeState(); state.teams = savedTeams; state.players = savedPlayers;`. For full-reset, which removes the teams, emit `io.emit('force-rejoin')` and have player.html set hasJoined=false and show the join screen.

findings.title: No host authorization, and '/' redirects to /host: any guest gets the game-master panel
findings.detail: Every host event (award-points, override-score, steal-execute, next-turn, reveal-answer, open-buzzer, set-rounds, start-game, host-spin, reset-game, full-reset; server.js:203-353) is accepted from any socket. server.js:364 redirects '/' to /host, so a guest who types the printed 'Network: http://10.0.0.235:PORT' without /player lands on the full controls. Reproduced (t_state.out T11): a player socket set team A to 99999 and then ran full-reset, which wiped all teams.
findings.fix: Generate a key at startup with `const HOST_KEY = crypto.randomBytes(3).toString('hex');` and print `http://IP:PORT/host?key=HOST_KEY`. host.html connects with `io({ auth: { hostKey: new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('key') } })`. On connection set `socket.data.isHost = socket.handshake.auth.hostKey === HOST_KEY` and `if (socket.data.isHost) socket.join('host')`. Guard host handlers with `if (!socket.data.isHost) return;`. Change server.js:364 to `res.redirect('/player')`. For the TV, use a separate read-only key or no key, since it only listens.

findings.title: The 5.5s spin timeout is never cancelled: a reset or Next Turn during a spin applies a stale result (and can lock the lobby)
findings.detail: server.js:229 and server.js:239 call setTimeout(() => processSegment(seg), 5500) without keeping the handle or checking state. Reproduced (t_state.out): T1, full-reset during a spin → 5.5s later phase='challenge' with teams [], after which create-team is rejected (server.js:184) and the lobby stays locked until another full reset. T2, reset-game during a spin → phase 'challenge' with the host page off the lobby. T3, Next Turn during team A's spin, then team B spins → events 'spin-start#6, turn-start, spin-start#5, spin-result:w6, spin-result:w5'. A's Dare result fired in the middle of B's spin and was then overwritten. The host's Next Turn button is always enabled (host.html:385).
findings.fix: Add `let spinTimer = null, spinSeq = 0;`. When spinning: `const seq = ++spinSeq; clearTimeout(spinTimer); spinTimer = setTimeout(() => { spinTimer = null; if (state.phase !== 'spinning' || seq !== spinSeq) return; processSegment(WHEEL_SEGMENTS[segIndex]); }, 5500);`. Call `clearTimeout(spinTimer); spinTimer = null; spinSeq++;` in reset-game, full-reset, start-game and next-turn. Reject next-turn while phase === 'spinning'. Combine spin-wheel and host-spin into one startSpin() function so the logic exists once.

findings.title: next-turn has no phase guard or duplicate guard: a double-tap skips a team, and it works in the lobby, after game end and with zero teams
findings.detail: server.js:306-334 runs in every phase. Reproduced (t_state.out): T4, two quick next-turn taps → current team 0→2, so team B lost its turn. T5a, next-turn in the lobby → phase 'playing' without start-game. T5b, next-turn after 'gameend' → phase 'playing', round 2 of 1, game resumed. T5c, zero teams → currentTeamIndex = (0+1)%0 = NaN (shown as null). The host's Next Turn button is a big always-enabled phone button (host.html:385), so double-taps will happen.
findings.fix: Add `state.turnId` (increment it on every turn change and include it in publicState). host.html sends `socket.emit('next-turn', { turnId: gameState.turnId })`. The server ignores the event when `turnId !== state.turnId`, when `!['challenge','hotseat','playing'].includes(state.phase)`, or when `state.teams.length === 0`. Optionally disable the button during 'spinning'.

findings.title: The printed LAN address can be the VPN or a virtual adapter, and no screen shows the real join URL
findings.detail: server.js:369-376 prints every non-internal IPv4 address in OS order. A server.log from an earlier run today on this machine showed 'Network: http://10.200.101.14:47613' (not the Wi-Fi adapter) before 'Network: http://10.0.0.235:47613' (Wi-Fi, 10.0.0.235/24, default gateway 10.0.0.1). The same code would also print 169.254.x link-local addresses and Hyper-V/WSL/Docker vEthernet 172.x addresses when those adapters are up. tv.html:263 and host.html:280/340 only say '/player', with no host:port, so guests depend on whoever reads the console. With a full-tunnel corporate VPN connected, LAN traffic may also be blocked (not verified for this VPN).
findings.fix: Pick one address. Skip `169.254.`, and skip interface names matching `/vEthernet|WSL|Hyper-V|VirtualBox|VMware|Docker|Loopback|Tailscale|ZeroTier|VPN|TAP|Cisco|AnyConnect|GlobalProtect|Zscaler|Bluetooth/i`. Prefer `/Wi-?Fi|Wireless|WLAN|Ethernet/i` and 192.168/16 or 10/8 ranges. Allow an override with `process.env.HOST_IP`. Expose `app.get('/api/info', (q, r) => r.json({ joinUrl: `http://${ip}:${PORT}/player` }))` (or emit it in 'wheel-segments'). Show the URL big, with a QR code, in the TV lobby and on the host page. Print the remaining candidates as 'other interfaces'. Tell the host to disconnect the VPN before the party.

findings.title: Windows Firewall will probably block phones: Wi-Fi profile is Public and there is no inbound rule for node.exe
findings.detail: Get-NetConnectionProfile shows Wi-Fi 'leysML' as NetworkCategory Public. All firewall profiles are Enabled, with DefaultInboundAction NotConfigured (Windows default: block). Get-NetFirewallApplicationFilter found no rule for C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe. The server binds 0.0.0.0 (server.js:367). The party Wi-Fi will be a new network, which Windows 11 also marks Public by default. NOT VERIFIED end-to-end, because traffic from this machine to its own IP skips the firewall. It needs a test from a real phone.
findings.fix: Before the party, set the network to Private with `Set-NetConnectionProfile -InterfaceAlias Wi-Fi -NetworkCategory Private` (admin), or add a rule with `New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'Christmas Chaos' -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 3000 -Action Allow -Profile Private,Public` (admin). Add a startup console hint saying that if phones cannot connect, the network should be set to Private. Do a dry run with one phone on the party Wi-Fi.

findings.title: A server restart or crash mid-game loses all teams and scores, and phones do not recover
findings.detail: State is only in memory (server.js:57). Reproduced (t_crash.out): before the restart phase 'playing' with A:500, B:0; after the restart phase 'lobby' with teams []. Phones reconnect automatically but stay in a joined-looking waiting screen with no teams, and they never rejoin (player.html:396). Recovery means recreating teams in the same order, re-entering scores with override and reloading every phone. This also makes the crash finding much worse.
findings.fix: Persist after every change. Use `function save(){ clearTimeout(saveT); saveT = setTimeout(() => fs.writeFile(SAVE, JSON.stringify({ ...state, players: strip(state.players) }), () => {}), 200); }` and call it inside a shared `broadcast()` that replaces the `io.emit('state-update', ...)` calls. On boot, `if (fs.existsSync(SAVE)) state = { ...makeState(), ...JSON.parse(...) }`, and if the phase was 'spinning' set it back to 'playing'. Keep SAVE outside public/ (for example `path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'christmas-chaos-save.json')`). Together with the persistent player id, phones restore themselves.

findings.title: remove-team works by array index: a double-tap deletes two teams, a bad payload deletes team 0, and the index shift leaves phones on the wrong team
findings.detail: server.js:191-201 splices by index and renumbers p.teamIndex on the server only. Reproduced (t_more.out M2): A,B,C,D plus two remove-team {teamIndex:1} → [A,D]. T13: remove-team {} → splice(undefined,1) removed team A. M6 (Edge): Carol joined C (index 2), then A was removed; the server moved her to C@1, but the phone keeps myTeamIndex=2 (player.html:394) and showed badge 'D'. On C's turn her SPIN button was hidden; on D's turn it was visible, and the tap was silently rejected (phase stayed 'playing'). Players on the removed team are deleted on the server but their phones still think they joined.
findings.fix: Give teams stable ids (`id: nextTeamId++`) and have players store teamId. remove-team takes `{ teamId }` and ignores ids that do not exist, which also makes a double-tap harmless. After any change to a player's team, `io.to(p.socketId).emit('you', p)` (or `need-join` for removed teams) so the phone takes its team from the server rather than its local myTeamIndex. currentTeamIndex can stay an index into teams, because teams are lobby-only.

findings.title: Regular trivia is handled exactly like ALL PLAY: every team can buzz, so the spinning team has no advantage
findings.detail: server.js:130-136 handles `seg.type === 'trivia' || seg.type === 'allplay'` the same way: buzzerOpen = true for everyone, and buzzer-press (server.js:242-251) does not check the team. Reproduced (t_more.out M3): on team A's 'Christmas Trivia' (w8), Bob from team B buzzed and won. 'ALL PLAY!' (w7) means nothing extra, and a team's own trivia spin can be stolen every time.
findings.fix: For 'trivia' set `state.buzzerTeam = state.currentTeamIndex` (or skip the buzzer: the current team answers by voice or typing, and the host can then 'open-buzzer' to steal). For 'allplay' set `state.buzzerTeam = null`. In buzzer-press add `if (state.buzzerTeam != null && player.teamIndex !== state.buzzerTeam) return;`.

findings.title: There is no server path for typed answers ('use a buzzer or type answers' is not implemented)
findings.detail: server.js handles only buzzer-press for player input. It has no 'submit-answer' (or similar) event, and player.html emits only join-game, spin-wheel and buzzer-press (player.html:396,527,532). Teams that cannot be heard in a noisy room, or ALL PLAY rounds where every team answers, have no way to send an answer.
findings.fix: Add `socket.on('submit-answer', ({ text }) => { if (state.phase !== 'challenge' && state.phase !== 'hotseat') return; const p = findPlayer(socket); if (!p) return; state.answers[p.teamId] = { text: String(text).slice(0, 80), by: p.name, at: Date.now() }; io.to('host').emit('answers', state.answers); io.emit('answer-count', Object.keys(state.answers).length); })`. Clear `state.answers` in next-turn and processSegment. The host marks each answer correct, which calls award-points.

findings.title: Answers (and the Sound It Out song) are sent to every client before the reveal
findings.detail: publicState() includes the full currentChallenge (server.js:116), and spin-result (server.js:136,148,156) and hotseat-question (server.js:290) broadcast it too, including answer, hint, songTitle and artist, to the TV and all phones. Reproduced (t_more.out M3): with answerRevealed=false, a player socket received answer='Todd Chester (played by Nicholas Guest)'. Because the server broadcasts everything, clients cannot keep the song secret either. The earlier client review captured the TV and teammates seeing the song (scratchpad/review/clients/tv_sounditout_leak.png, player_teammate_sees_song.png).
findings.fix: Add `function publicChallenge(c){ if (!c) return null; const { answer, songTitle, artist, ...rest } = c; return state.answerRevealed ? c : rest; }` and use it in publicState, spin-result and hotseat-question. Send the full challenge only to the host: `io.to('host').emit('host-challenge', c)`. For Sound It Out, pick one hummer on the current team and send the song only to them: `io.to(hummer.socketId).emit('secret-song', { songTitle, artist })`.

findings.title: Double Down doubles the next award to any team (including penalties) and survives Next Turn
findings.detail: server.js:268 doubles and clears on the first award-points call regardless of team or sign. next-turn (server.js:306-330) never clears doubleDownActive. Reproduced (t_state.out T6): team C hit Double Down, the host pressed Next Turn, dd stayed true, and +100 to team B became 200. A -50 penalty becomes -100 and uses up C's double. Steal ignores it.
findings.fix: In processSegment set `state.doubleDownTeam = state.currentTeamIndex` instead of a bool. In award-points: `if (state.doubleDownTeam === teamIndex && pts > 0) { pts *= 2; state.doubleDownTeam = null; }`. In next-turn, clear it once the bonus turn ends: keep it across the DD re-spin, which leaves phase 'playing' with the same team, and clear it when currentTeamIndex changes. Expose `doubleDownActive: state.doubleDownTeam != null` in publicState.

findings.title: Steal can be repeated, works in any phase, creates points from nothing, allows stealing from yourself, and trusts the client's indices
findings.detail: server.js:273-278 has no phase or segment check, no once-only flag and no from !== to check. It always adds 100 even when the victim has less. Reproduced (t_state.out T10): stealing from B with 30 left B:0 and gave A:100 (70 points created); a self-steal on C (0 points) gave C:100. Each extra tap on 'Steal 100!' (host.html:483) steals again. Bad indices crash the server.
findings.fix: `if (state.phase !== 'challenge' || state.currentChallenge?.type !== 'steal' || state.stealDone) return; const to = state.currentTeamIndex; if (!validTeam(fromTeamIndex) || fromTeamIndex === to) return; const amt = Math.min(100, state.teams[fromTeamIndex].score); state.teams[fromTeamIndex].score -= amt; state.teams[to].score += amt; state.stealDone = true;` Reset stealDone in processSegment. Ignore the toTeamIndex the client sends.

findings.title: start-game is accepted in any phase: mid-game it resets the round and keeps the old challenge
findings.detail: server.js:208-216 checks only teams.length. Reproduced (t_more.out M4): during a STEAL challenge, start-game → phase 'playing', round 1, current team 0, scores kept, currentChallenge still set. The TV then shows the old challenge in 'playing' (tv.html shows currentChallenge whenever the phase is not spinning). During a spin, the uncancelled timer then flips the phase to 'challenge'.
findings.fix: Add `if (state.phase !== 'lobby' || state.teams.length < 2) return;`. Clear currentChallenge, currentSegment, buzzerOpen, buzzerWinner, doubleDown and the hot-seat fields, and cancel spinTimer.

findings.title: Non-numeric points, score or rounds poison state with NaN (scores show null forever; the game never ends)
findings.detail: server.js:267-269: Number('abc') = NaN and Math.max(0, NaN) = NaN, so the score is NaN, sent as null, and every later award stays NaN. server.js:338 has the same problem. server.js:204: Math.max(1, Math.min(6, NaN)) = NaN, so `round > NaN` (server.js:312) is never true. Reproduced: T7 'A:null' even after +100; T8 round 11 with totalRounds null, still 'playing'. The host UI sends numbers, so this needs a crafted or buggy payload, which is easy without host auth.
findings.fix: `const pts = Math.trunc(Number(points)); if (!Number.isFinite(pts) || Math.abs(pts) > 10000) return;`. Use the same check for score. For rounds: `const r = Number(rounds); if (!Number.isInteger(r)) return; state.totalRounds = Math.max(state.round, Math.min(6, Math.max(1, r)));`.

findings.title: join-game and create-team accept empty names, HTML names, unbounded length and invalid team indices
findings.detail: server.js:179 stores name and teamIndex unchecked, and server.js:186 stores teamName unchecked. Reproduced: M5, name '' with teamIndex '0' (a string) was accepted, and that player can never spin because `'0' !== 0` (server.js:221). T15, teamIndex 42 was accepted and won the buzzer as team 'Unknown' while in the lobby. A name of `` ran script on /host (t_reconnect.out R4; host.html renders p.name with innerHTML). Names can be close to 1 MB (the socket.io default maxHttpBufferSize) and are re-sent in every state-update.
findings.fix: `const name = String(name ?? '').replace(/[<>]/g, '').trim().slice(0, 20); const ti = Number(teamIndex); if (!name || !validTeam(ti)) return socket.emit('join-error', 'Pick a name and team');`. Apply the same cleanup to teamName (max 24 characters, reject duplicates). Also escape on the client (textContent instead of innerHTML templates).

findings.title: Buzzer events ignore the phase, and a team that answered wrong is never locked out
findings.detail: open-buzzer and close-buzzer (server.js:295-304) work in lobby, gameend, dare and so on. buzzer-press (server.js:242) only checks buzzerOpen; T15 shows a win in the lobby. After a wrong answer the host re-opens with open-buzzer, which resets buzzerWinner for everyone, so the same player can win again straight away. processSegment only resets the buzzer for trivia, not for the other segment types.
findings.fix: Accept open-buzzer only when `state.phase === 'challenge' && ['trivia','allplay'].includes(state.currentSegment?.type)`. Keep `state.buzzLocked = new Set()` of team ids: add the winner's team when the host marks the answer wrong or re-opens, and reject buzzer-press from locked teams. Reset the set in processSegment and next-turn.

findings.title: A double-tap on hot-seat 'Next Q' skips a question; hot seat never reuses used questions
findings.detail: server.js:280-293 increments hotSeatIndex on every event with no expected index, so two taps skip a question (found by reading the code; not run, because it needs a random Hot Seat spin). pickHotSeat (server.js:93-105) does not reuse questions the way pickQuestion does. If the christmas+popculture pool is used up (more likely if Play Again stops repeating questions), the result is phase 'hotseat' with a null challenge and hotSeatTotal 0.
findings.fix: Client sends `{ index: gameState.hotSeatIndex }` and the server ignores the event `if (index !== state.hotSeatIndex)`. In pickHotSeat, if the pool has fewer than count questions, drop those categories' ids from usedQuestionIds and rebuild the pool, as pickQuestion does.

findings.title: Adding or removing a team silently overwrites the host's manual round count
findings.detail: server.js:187 and server.js:199 always call recommendedRounds(). Reproduced (t_state.out T12): the host set 6 rounds, added team C, and rounds went back to 4. A late team arriving after the host set the length of a 60-75 minute game resets it.
findings.fix: Set `state.roundsManual = true` in set-rounds, and only auto-recommend while `!state.roundsManual`. Clear the flag in full-reset.

findings.title: award-points works in the lobby and after game end, and there is no undo
findings.detail: server.js:265-271 only checks that the team exists. Points can change after the final standings are shown, and a mistaken or double tap on +100 (host.html:477) can only be fixed by typing a score into Override.
findings.fix: Reject when `state.phase === 'lobby' || state.phase === 'gameend'`. Keep `state.lastAward = { teamIndex, delta }` (the delta actually applied after the 0 floor) and add an 'undo-award' event that reverses it once.

findings.title: 'Play Again' clears used question and dare ids, so game 2 repeats the same questions
findings.detail: reset-game (server.js:343-346) rebuilds state with makeState(), which resets usedQuestionIds and usedDareIds (server.js:46-47). With 40/25/25 questions and 25 dares, a second game at the same party repeats content soon.
findings.fix: In reset-game keep `state.usedQuestionIds` and `state.usedDareIds` from the previous state; the existing recycle logic in pickQuestion and pickDare already handles running out.

findings.title: A player can switch teams mid-game by re-emitting join-game
findings.detail: server.js:178-181 accepts join-game in every phase and overwrites teamIndex. A player can move to the team whose turn it is to spin, or to another team to buzz for it. With socket.id identity the same person can also appear twice (old ghost plus new entry) after a reconnect.
findings.fix: Once phase !== 'lobby', allow join-game only for new players (or players whose stored team no longer exists). Team changes after the start go through the host (a 'move-player' host event).

findings.title: Port already in use crashes with a raw stack trace
findings.detail: server.listen (server.js:367) has no 'error' handler. If an earlier instance is still running on the port, Node throws EADDRINUSE as an unhandled 'error' event and the host sees a stack trace minutes before the party. Standard Node behaviour; not run here.
findings.fix: `server.on('error', e => { if (e.code === 'EADDRINUSE') { console.error(`Port ${PORT} is busy - close the other Christmas Chaos window or run with PORT=3001`); process.exit(1); } throw e; });`

findings.title: Tied teams get different medals at game end
findings.detail: server.js:314 sorts by score only, so tied teams come out in array order and the host, TV and phones give them different medals. For a competitive family game a tie should be shown, or decided with a tiebreak question.
findings.fix: Compute ranks with ties: `sorted.forEach((t, i) => t.rank = i && t.score === sorted[i-1].score ? sorted[i-1].rank : i + 1)` and send rank. Optionally go to a 'tiebreak' phase that runs one ALL PLAY question between the tied leaders.

result.summary:
Read-only, line-by-line review of public/tv.html, host.html, player.html and css/style.css. I ran the real server on PORT=3487 and drove it with socket.io-client plus headless Edge (Playwright), using either the real socket or a stubbed one, then stopped the server. All scripts and screenshots are in C:/Users/mleys/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d489c8c283eb5306/1f6a997f-d385-4b62-994e-3617bc11ff4c/scratchpad/review/clients/ (sock1.js, pw1_tv.js, pw1b_tvend.js, pw2_host_player.js, pw3_real.js, pw4_extra.js, *.png). No project file was changed.

The wheel math is correct. offset = 360-(i+0.5)*30 lines segment i up with the top pointer: 26 out of 26 stubbed spins and 4 out of 4 real end-to-end spins stopped mid-segment on the segment the server picked. Every event name the clients emit is handled by the server. The TV just ignores 'spin-result' and 'game-started' and never listens for 'hotseat-complete'.

Five problems would break the party:
1. **Phones lose their player after reconnecting.** The server deletes a player on disconnect, and the phone never re-sends join-game. After a screen lock or Wi-Fi blip the phone looks normal but its SPIN and BUZZ buttons do nothing.
2. **"Play Again (keep teams)" / "Reset Scores" wipes every player on the server.** No phone can spin or buzz in the next game.
3. **The TV game-over screen never appears.** The TV goes blank at the end.
4. **The Sound It Out song title is shown on the TV and on every phone of the performing team** before anyone guesses.
5. **The host cannot see a trivia answer without revealing it to everyone.**

Other verified problems: team names and player names are inserted as raw HTML on all three screens. A crafted name ran a script on the host page that awarded 11,900 points in about a second. The phone keeps its old team number after the host removes a team. Next Turn has no guard: a double-click skips a team, and pressing it mid-spin jams the game. The TV keeps showing the previous answer and song title into the next team's spin. The TV Double Down banner can never appear. The host page is unusable on a phone (110px content column). There is no typed-answer input. Plain trivia is open to every team, so it plays exactly like ALL PLAY.

findings.title: A phone that reconnects becomes a 'ghost': it shows the game normally but SPIN and BUZZ silently do nothing
findings.detail: server.js:355-357 deletes state.players[socket.id] on disconnect. socket.io then reconnects with a NEW socket.id. player.html has no socket.on('connect') handler and never re-sends join-game. hasJoined, myName and myTeamIndex (player.html:326-329) stay set, so the page keeps rendering the game. Verified with the real server (pw4_extra.js and sock1.js): after socket.io.engine.close() the id changed, the server's players list was [], and the phone still showed "It's YOUR team's turn!" with the spin button visible. Tapping SPIN emitted nothing (no spin-start), and buzzer-press was ignored. doSpin (player.html:525-528) leaves the button disabled forever with no message. doBuzzer (530-534) still shows the 'Buzzed!' toast. An iOS screen lock longer than about 45 seconds (server ping timeout), switching apps, or a Wi-Fi blip all trigger this, so over a 60-75 minute party almost every phone will hit it.
findings.fix: In player.html add: socket.on('connect', () => { if (hasJoined) socket.emit('join-game', { name: myName, teamIndex: indexOfTeamName(savedTeamName) }); }). Store the team NAME and look its index up in the latest state, because indexes shift. In the state-update handler, derive identity from the server: const me = state.players.find(p => p.id === socket.id). If hasJoined && !me, re-emit join-game, or return to the join screen if the team is gone. Show a 'Reconnecting…' banner on socket 'disconnect'. Re-enable the spin and buzz buttons after about 3 seconds if no spin-start or buzzer-winner arrives. Better, server side: identify players by a stable playerId kept in localStorage (crypto.randomUUID is unavailable over plain-HTTP LAN, so use Math.random) and mark them offline on disconnect instead of deleting them.

findings.title: 'Play Again (keep teams)' and 'Reset Scores' delete every player on the server, while every phone still says 'You're in!'
findings.detail: host.html:268 and :394 emit reset-game. server.js:342-348 runs state = makeState() and restores only teams, so players becomes {}. Verified (sock1.js [C]): players went from Ann,Bob to []. player.html still has hasJoined=true and shows the waiting screen (verified for full reset in pw2: waiting-screen visible, badge 'Elves' with empty teams). In the second game, spin-wheel and buzzer-press are rejected for everyone (server.js:220-221, 244-245). Only the host's backup spin works.
findings.fix: Server: in reset-game keep the players (const savedPlayers = state.players; …; state.players = savedPlayers). Client: the same re-sync as the reconnect finding. In state-update, if hasJoined and you are not in state.players, re-join by team name, or show the join screen with a 'The host reset the game, please re-join' message. On full-reset (teams empty), clear hasJoined, myTeamIndex and the badge and show the join screen.

findings.title: The TV 'Game Over' screen can never become visible, so the TV goes blank at the climax
findings.detail: tv.html:180-186 sets #end-screen { display:none } in its id rule. show('end-screen') (tv.html:397, 522, 574) only removes a 'hidden' class, which the element never had, so it stays display:none. Meanwhile the lobby and game screens are hidden. Verified (pw1b_tvend.js): after the real game-end + state-update sequence, end-screen computed display = none, lobby none, game none, even though end-results held 219 characters of HTML. Screenshot tv_gameend.png shows an empty main area and a stale header ('Round 3 of 3', "Reindeer's turn"). Also, on a TV refresh at gameend the results are empty (verified), because they are only rendered in the 'game-end' event handler (tv.html:573-581), not from state.
findings.fix: tv.html:180: change to #end-screen { display:flex; … } and give the element class="hidden" at line 290. In the state-update gameend branch (tv.html:521-522), render the sorted results from state.teams so a refresh works, and set round-label to 'Final scores' and turn-banner to ''.

findings.area: tv.html / player.html – Sound It Out secrecy
findings.title: The Sound It Out song title is displayed on the TV and on every phone of the guessing team before any guess
findings.detail: tv.html:443-445 always fills and shows #sound-title with '🎵 <songTitle> — <artist>' in big gold text. Verified: visible before any reveal (tv_sounditout_leak.png). player.html:481-483 shows the title to EVERY member of the current team (isMyTurn is a team check), and those teammates are the guessers. Verified: the performer's and the teammate's phones both show 'Hum or whistle: "All I Want for Christmas Is You"' (player_teammate_sees_song.png). The root cause is also server side: spin-result and state-update broadcast the full challenge, including songTitle and answer (and every trivia answer), to all sockets (sock1.js [D]).
findings.fix: TV: only show #sound-title when state.answerRevealed is true. Phones: add a performer concept. In spin-wheel the server records performerId = socket.id (for host-spin, pick a connected player on that team), strips songTitle, artist and answer from publicState()/spin-result, and sends them only with io.to(performerId).emit('secret', …) and to a host room. player.html then shows the title only when state.performerId === socket.id, and other teammates see 'Your teammate is humming — guess!'. Interim client-only option: on the current team's phones, hide the title behind a press-and-hold 'Performer only – peek' button.

findings.title: The host cannot see the answer privately. It stays hidden until Reveal, which shows it to everyone at the same moment
findings.detail: host.html:641-643 writes ch.answer into #ch-answer but keeps class 'challenge-a', and host.html:124-134 makes that display:none unless '.shown'. The only way to make it visible is Reveal (host.html:367/472), which broadcasts it to the TV and all phones (server.js:257-263). Verified: with a trivia question and Ann buzzed in, #ch-answer text = 'Rudolph' but computed display none (host_before_reveal.png). This applies to trivia, ALL PLAY and all 5 Hot Seat questions. Sound It Out is the exception: the host does see the song, via the hint line (host.html:620).
findings.fix: Always show the answer on the host page with a private style, e.g. in updateChallenge: else if (ch.answer) { ansEl.textContent = '🔒 Answer (only you see this): ' + ch.answer; ansEl.className = 'challenge-a shown private'; }. Style .private with a dashed border, and relabel the button 'Reveal to everyone'.

findings.title: After the host removes a team, the phone's cached myTeamIndex points at the wrong team
findings.detail: server.js:191-198 renumbers players (p.teamIndex--) when a lower-index team is removed, but player.html sets myTeamIndex once in joinGame (393) and never resyncs it. Verified (pw4_extra.js): after removing team 0, the server record was teamIndex 1 while the client still had myTeamIndex 2, and the '(you)' marker disappeared. sock1.js [A]: after the host added another team, the phone treated team 2's turn as its own and its SPIN was rejected. On the player's real turn the spin button is hidden (isMyTurn, player.html:429). Players on the removed team are deleted on the server but stay 'joined' on the phone. The join screen also selects by index (player.html:358, 369, 378-383), so if the host edits teams while someone is choosing, they can silently join a different team.
findings.fix: In the state-update handler: const me = state.players.find(p => p.id === socket.id); if (me) myTeamIndex = me.teamIndex; else if (hasJoined) send the user back to the join screen. On the join screen, store the selected team's name rather than its index, and resolve the index when sending join-game.

findings.title: Team and player names are injected into innerHTML. A crafted name ran a script on the host page that awarded itself 11,900 points in about a second
findings.detail: Raw ${t.name} or ${p.name} inside innerHTML templates: tv.html:408, 516, 578; host.html:505, 517, 532, 533, 544, 561, 585, 678; player.html:371, 421, 568. Player names come from any phone. maxlength=20 (player.html:255) is client-only, and the server stores names unchecked (server.js:179). Any socket can also emit create-team in the lobby (server.js:183). Verified on the real server (pw3_real.js): a team named ran on the host, the TV (twice) and the player join screen. A late joiner named ran on the host page, and because every award re-renders the players list, it looped: Reindeer went from 0 to 11,900 in about a second. Even harmless names containing '<' break the layout. Dare and hint text is also injected raw (tv.html:437, 462; host.html:615; player.html:479). That data is currently clean (no <, > or & found).
findings.fix: Add a helper to each page: const esc = s => String(s ?? '').replace(/[&<>"']/g, c => ({'&':'&','<':'<','>':'>','"':'"',"'":'''}[c])); and use ${esc(t.name)} or ${esc(p.name)} at every line listed, plus the dare title, description and hint. Also trim and length-cap names on the server in join-game and create-team.

findings.title: Next Turn has no guard: a double-click skips a team, and pressing it mid-spin leaves the game stuck in an invisible challenge
findings.detail: host.html:385/495-497 emit next-turn with no debounce and no phase check, and the button stays enabled while the wheel spins (verified in pw2). Verified on the real server (pw4_extra.js): a double-click on Next Turn moved currentTeamIndex from 0 to 2. Pressing Next Turn during a host spin made the pending processSegment timeout (server.js:229/239) fire for the NEXT team. The result was phase 'challenge', currentSegment null and a challenge set. The TV shows 'Waiting for next spin…', the host shows 'Waiting for spin…', the spin button is disabled, and only another Next Turn recovers.
findings.fix: host.html: disable the Next Turn button while state.phase === 'spinning', and after clicking it until a state-update arrives with a changed currentTeamIndex or round (or a 1-second cooldown). Add confirm() if no points were awarded this turn. Server: ignore next-turn while phase === 'spinning', and send a turn id that the client echoes back so duplicates are dropped.

findings.title: The previous turn's revealed answer, song title, props and hot-seat counter stay on the TV through the next team's turn and spin
findings.detail: The 'playing && !currentChallenge' branch (tv.html:527-530) and the spin-start handler (535-541) reset only the label and text. They never hide #challenge-answer-box, #sound-title, #dare-props or #hotseat-progress, and showChallenge (the only reset) is not called. Verified (pw1_tv.js, tv_stale_during_next_spin.png): after a Sound It Out turn and Next Turn, the TV shows 'Spin the wheel!' with the '✓ All I Want for Christmas Is You' box and the big song title still visible, and they remain while the next team's wheel spins.
findings.fix: Factor a resetChallengePanel() out of showChallenge (tv.html:422-426) and call it in the playing/no-challenge branch and at the top of the spin-start handler.

findings.title: Double Down is invisible on the TV: the banner can never show, and every 'Double Down' message branch is dead code
findings.detail: tv.html:199-211 sets #double-down-banner { display:none } and shows it only via '.show', but the JS (tv.html:503-505) only toggles the 'hidden' class, so the banner stays display:none. Verified: doubleDownActive=true gives computed display none. The server delivers Double Down with currentChallenge = null (server.js:160-163). The TV state-update therefore shows 'Spin the wheel!' with an empty label (verified end to end: after landing on Double Down the TV label was ''). The doubledown branches in tv.html:455, host.html:626 and player.html:492 can never run, because each is guarded by a !challenge or !ch early return. The host shows 'Waiting for spin…' (verified).
findings.fix: tv.html:199: remove display:none from #double-down-banner, since the .hidden class already handles it. Handle the segment without a challenge: in tv.html state-update, if (state.currentSegment?.effect === 'doubledown' && state.phase === 'playing') show the label '💫 Double Down!' and the explanatory text. Do the same in host updateChallenge and player updateGameScreen before the !ch early return.

findings.title: The host page is unusable on a phone: a fixed 280px sidebar leaves a 110px column for the game controls
findings.detail: host.html:26-43: .host-body is a flex row and .host-left is width:280px; flex-shrink:0, with no media query. A host walking around judging dares will likely use a phone. Verified at 390x844 (host_phone_390.png): left panel 280px, main panel 110px, and the question renders one word per line. The award buttons, Reveal and Next Turn are far below the fold.
findings.fix: Add @media (max-width: 760px) { .host-body { flex-direction: column; } .host-left { width: auto; border-right: 0; } } and consider putting #host-game (Reveal, Award, Next Turn) first on small screens, e.g. with order:-1.

findings.title: Players cannot type answers. Only a buzzer exists, although typed answers are a stated requirement
findings.detail: The only input in player.html is #name-input (line 255). Verified in pw2: the page's answer inputs are 'name-input' only. There is no answer field, no submit event, and no host view of submissions.
findings.fix: Add an answer form to #game-screen, shown while phase === 'challenge' for trivia/allplay (and for the hot-seat team), that emits 'submit-answer' {text}. The server should store it per team and send it only to the host, and the host page lists submissions with ✓/✗ buttons that call award-points. Lock submissions when the host reveals.

findings.title: On a team's own trivia spin every team gets the buzzer, so regular trivia plays exactly like ALL PLAY
findings.detail: player.html:464-471 shows the buzzer to all players whenever buzzerOpen && (seg.type === 'trivia' || 'allplay'), and the server opens the buzzer for both (server.js:130-136). Verified: on Elves' own Christmas Trivia turn, a Reindeer phone's buzzer was visible. Six of the 12 wheel segments are trivia, so the team that spun gets no advantage, and the ALL PLAY segment means nothing.
findings.fix: Client: showBuzzer = state.buzzerOpen && (seg.type === 'allplay' || (seg.type === 'trivia' && isMyTurn)). Better, let the team that spun answer alone, and only on a wrong answer the host clicks 'Open to all' (a new event). The server must enforce the same rule in buzzer-press.

findings.title: The TV and host only say 'Players join at: /player'. Guests are never shown the host's IP address or a QR code
findings.detail: tv.html:263 (the #lobby-qr element contains no QR code) and host.html:279-281/340 show only a path. The LAN URL is computed only in the server console (server.js:369-376). At a family party, nobody can type a path without the IP.
findings.fix: Add a server endpoint (e.g. GET /api/info returning http://<lan-ip>:<port>/player from the existing os.networkInterfaces() loop). The TV lobby renders it in large text plus a QR code; serve a QR library locally, since the LAN may have no internet. Interim: show location.host when the TV is opened via the LAN IP.

findings.title: There is no keep-awake handling on any page. Phones auto-lock between turns, and a laptop driving the TV may blank its display
findings.detail: No navigator.wakeLock, NoSleep-style video or similar exists in any page (verified by search in pw2). On phones, auto-lock suspends the page, which feeds directly into the ghost-player bug. Note that the Screen Wake Lock API needs a secure context, so it is unavailable on phones loading http://192.168.x.x. It works for a TV page opened as http://localhost on the host laptop. Whether a laptop display actually sleeps depends on its OS power settings (unverified).
findings.fix: tv.html: request navigator.wakeLock.request('screen') on load, re-acquire on visibilitychange, and wrap it in try/catch. Phones: fixing reconnects (critical finding 1) is the real cure. Optionally start a muted, looping, playsinline 1-second video on the Join tap as a NoSleep fallback. Add a hint 'Keep this page open – set Auto-Lock to Never during the game'.

findings.title: Reveal, Open Buzzer and Close Buzzer are live in every phase, producing '✓ —' on the TV and 'BUZZ IN NOW!' with no buzzer on any phone
findings.detail: host.html:366-371 never disables these buttons. Verified: during spinning they were all enabled. Reveal with no answer (a dare, steal, or before a spin) makes the server send '—' (server.js:260), and the TV shows and keeps '✓ —' (pw1 [reveal-none]). Open Buzzer during a dare, Sound It Out or idle makes the TV show '🔔 BUZZ IN NOW!' (tv.html:474-476) while the phones show no buzzer (player.html:465). Verified for all three cases.
findings.fix: In host state-update: btn-reveal.disabled = !(ch && ch.answer) || state.answerRevealed; open and close buzzer enabled only when seg.type is 'trivia' or 'allplay' and phase === 'challenge'. Make the TV updateBuzzer use the same segment-type condition as player.html:465.

findings.title: The host panel never shows who buzzed in, only a 4-second toast
findings.detail: state.buzzerWinner is ignored by updateChallenge (host.html:592-647). The only display is the toast at host.html:702-704. Verified: with Ann buzzed in, the panel shows nothing (host_before_reveal.png). If the host looks away while judging, they must read the TV.
findings.fix: Add a #ch-buzz line in #current-challenge-box: state.buzzerWinner ? `🏆 ${esc(name)} (${esc(team)})` : (state.buzzerOpen ? '🔔 Buzzer open' : '🔕 Buzzer closed'). Highlight that team's award row.

findings.title: Score-override inputs are rebuilt on every state-update, wiping what the host is typing
findings.detail: renderOverride (host.html:539-549) runs on every state-update (692), including player joins, disconnects and buzzes. Verified: typing 999 then receiving an unrelated state-update reset the value to '250' and removed focus. Phones dropping and reconnecting make this frequent.
findings.fix: Skip re-rendering while document.activeElement is inside #override-list, or update only the input values that are not focused. Render the list only when the team count changes.

findings.title: Steal can be applied repeatedly (a double-click steals 200), and the steal panel stays after stealing
findings.detail: stealFrom (host.html:481-485) has no once-guard, and the panel re-renders while the segment is still steal (621-625). Verified: a double-click emitted steal-execute twice, and #steal-ui stayed display:block. The award panel also offers '+100' to every team during a steal turn (segment.points=100), inviting double counting.
findings.fix: Track stealDoneForTurn on the client (reset on turn-start) and hide #steal-ui after one steal. Better, the server marks the challenge resolved and rejects repeats. Hide the +base award buttons for the steal segment.

findings.title: After the last Hot Seat question the TV keeps showing it, and the host shows 'Waiting for spin…'
findings.detail: The server sets phase 'challenge' with currentChallenge null and emits 'hotseat-complete' (server.js:284-287). The TV has no hotseat-complete listener, and its state-update branch skips 'challenge' phase with a null challenge. Verified: the TV still shows Q5 and 'Question 5 of 5'. The host (host.html:607-611) shows 'Waiting for spin…' while it should be prompting for awards (verified).
findings.fix: TV: socket.on('hotseat-complete', …) → show '🔥 Hot Seat complete!' and hide the progress line. Host: in updateChallenge, treat seg.type === 'hotseat' && !ch as 'Hot Seat complete – award +25 per correct answer'.

findings.title: A refreshed or reconnected TV shows the wheel at rest on a segment boundary, not on the chosen segment; reconnecting mid-spin freezes the wheel
findings.detail: buildWheel (tv.html:325-362) recreates #wheel-group with no transform, and state-update never restores the rotation from state.currentSegment. At rest the pointer sits on the STEAL / Christmas Trivia boundary (measured fill #0e6655). A TV refreshed mid-spin shows 'Spin the wheel to begin!' with a static wheel (verified). If 'wheel-segments' arrives during a spin (socket reconnect), spinToTarget keeps animating the detached old group captured at line 374. Verified: after the spin the visible group's transform is null while currentWheelDeg = 1665.
findings.fix: After buildWheel, set the transform to rotate(currentWheelDeg). In state-update, when state.currentSegment exists and no spin is animating, compute its index (segments.findIndex(s => s.id === seg.id)) and set rotate(360 - (i+0.5)*30). In frame(), look up #wheel-group on each frame instead of capturing it once.

findings.title: The hot-seat phone can briefly display the NEXT question's answer
findings.detail: The server emits 'hotseat-question' before the state-update that carries answerRevealed=false (server.js:283-292). player.html:595-601 merges the new question into the cached gameState, which still has answerRevealed:true from the previous reveal, and re-renders. Verified DOM state between the two messages: 'Q2/5: Q two?' with '✓ Answer: Answer TWO' visible. Whether a frame paints before the next message is timing-dependent. Same pattern at host.html:706-712.
findings.fix: In both hotseat-question handlers set gameState.answerRevealed = false before re-rendering, or drop the handlers and rely on the state-update that follows.

findings.title: A reload or accidental pull-to-refresh loses the player's identity, and they must re-type their name and re-pick a team
findings.detail: Identity lives only in memory (player.html:326-329). There is no localStorage and no overscroll-behavior, so Android Chrome and iOS 15+ pull-to-refresh reload the page mid-game.
findings.fix: Save {name, teamName, playerId} to localStorage on join (in try/catch) and auto-rejoin on load if that team still exists. Add html, body { overscroll-behavior-y: none; } to the player page.

findings.title: Trivia hints are shown on the TV immediately with the question, and some nearly give the answer away
