findings.detail: tv.html:461-463 appends 'Hint: …' as soon as the question appears. Example: 'In Home Alone, what is the main character's first name?' with the hint 'His last name is McCallister'. The host has no control over when it appears.
findings.fix: Only render the hint when a new state.hintShown flag is true, toggled by a 'Show hint' host button (perhaps at reduced points).

findings.title: Long toasts overflow off both sides of small phones
findings.detail: style.css:293 sets #toast { white-space: nowrap }. Verified at 360px: '🏆 Great-Aunt Margaret from your team got it!' spans x = -24 to 384, so both ends are cut off (player_toast_long_360.png).
findings.fix: Use white-space: normal; max-width: calc(100vw - 32px); text-align: center; border-radius: 16px.

findings.title: Team colors used as text fail contrast on the navy background, down to 2.17:1
findings.detail: Team names are drawn in t.color on #0a1628 at tv.html:577, host.html:678 and player.html:568. Computed ratios: #1a5276 2.17, #8e44ad 3.09, #7D6608 3.26, #c0392b 3.33, #1a7a3c 3.36, #2471a3 3.42, #117a65 3.45, #d35400 4.35. All fail 4.5:1 for the small text on the host and phone end screens, and team 8 fails even the large-text 3:1 on the TV. Green #1a7a3c and teal #117a65 are also hard to tell apart as dots.
findings.fix: Keep names white and use the team color only for a dot or border, or lighten the palette for text, e.g. mix with white to reach at least 4.5:1. Replace teal with a clearly distinct hue.

findings.title: Unlabelled inputs, controls only usable by mouse or touch, no live announcements
findings.detail: host.html:304-308 tabs are <div onclick> (verified: tagName DIV, tabIndex -1). player.html:369 team options are <div onclick> and cannot be reached by keyboard or switch access. #name-input (player.html:254-255) uses a <div class=form-label> rather than <label for>, and #new-team-input (host.html:287) has only a placeholder. The remove '✕' button (host.html:506) has no aria-label or confirmation. Turn changes, buzz results and toasts have no aria-live. style.css:270 removes the input outline (a gold border remains).
findings.fix: Use <button> for tabs and team options (or role=radio with tabindex=0 and a keydown handler). Use <label for=…>. Add aria-label="Remove team X" plus confirm(). Add role=status aria-live=polite to #toast and #turn-status.

findings.title: The player viewport disables pinch-zoom, which hurts low-vision relatives
findings.detail: player.html:5 sets maximum-scale=1, user-scalable=no. Android Chrome honours this. iOS Safari has ignored it since iOS 10. Double-tap zoom is already handled by body { touch-action: manipulation } (player.html:16), so the zoom lock adds nothing.
findings.fix: Use <meta name=viewport content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> and keep touch-action: manipulation.

findings.title: In the lobby the host cannot see who has joined, and Start Game allows teams with no players
findings.detail: renderPlayers only runs in the in-game branch (host.html:682-699). The lobby branch (666-669) shows team names only. A team with 0 players can never spin from a phone.
findings.fix: In renderLobbyTeams, show the player count and names per team, and warn on Start if any team has 0 players.

findings.title: The TV wheel is small and its labels are about 9.5px, with left-side labels upside down
findings.detail: tv.html:271 fixes the SVG at 380px, about 35% of a 1080p screen. Segment text uses font-size 5.5 in a 220-unit viewBox, about 9.5 CSS px (measured). Labels are rotated radially (tv.html:345-347), so the left half reads upside down (tv_stale_during_next_spin.png). Score names are 0.95rem. Much of this is hard to read from a sofa.
findings.fix: Size the wheel with CSS (width/height: min(70vh, 45vw)), raise the label font size to about 9-10 units and the challenge text to clamp(1.3rem, 2vw, 2.4rem). Flip labels whose mid-angle is between 90° and 270° by adding 180°.

findings.title: The 'Spinning…' overlay is off-center because the pulse animation overrides translateX(-50%)
findings.detail: tv.html:165-177 centers with transform: translateX(-50%) but also runs animation: pulse, whose keyframes set transform: scale(...) (style.css:306-309) and replace the translate. Measured: the overlay center is at x 1174 vs tv-main center 1090.
findings.fix: Center with left:0; right:0; text-align:center (no transform), or wrap the text in an inner span that carries the pulse animation.

findings.title: The buzzer fires on click (on release) and gives no haptic or sound feedback; iOS may not show the :active press effect
findings.detail: player.html:303 uses onclick, which fires on release, so a player holding their finger down loses the race. There is no navigator.vibrate and no audio anywhere (verified). iOS Safari doesn't support vibrate at all, and audio there must be unlocked by a user gesture. iOS Safari also applies :active (style.css:215-218, 247-250) only when a touchstart listener exists (known WebKit behavior, not tested on a device).
findings.fix: Use buzzer.addEventListener('pointerdown', doBuzzer). Call navigator.vibrate?.(80) where supported. Add document.addEventListener('touchstart', () => {}, {passive: true}) for :active on iOS. For TV sounds (wheel ticks, buzz), add a 'Click to start' overlay on the TV that unlocks audio and enters fullscreen.

findings.title: Small text and toast glitches
findings.detail: host.html:478 shows '+-50 pts' for deductions and the un-doubled value during Double Down (verified '+-50 pts → Elves'). The toast() helpers (host.html:430-435, player.html:351-356) never clear the previous timer, so a round-start toast is replaced by turn-start and the later toast is hidden early. "${name}'s turn" renders 'Elves's turn'. The TV highlights team 0 as active in the lobby (tv.html:406). The TV's 'spin-result' handler is a no-op (543-545). Fonts load through a Google Fonts @import (style.css:1), so without internet the headings fall back to the system cursive font.
findings.fix: Format awards as (points > 0 ? '+' : '') + points, using the doubled value. In toast(), clearTimeout(window.__toastT) before setting a new timer. Use 'Up now: Elves'. Highlight the active team only when phase !== 'lobby'. Remove the dead handler. Self-host the two fonts.

result.summary:
GAME DESIGN REVIEW of Christmas Chaos (read-only; no project files touched). The core loop works: a player spins from their phone, the TV wheel animates in sync, and the host judges. As a game show, though, it has four critical problems.

1. **Sound It Out shows the answer to the people guessing it.** The song title appears on the TV and on every phone of the active team.
2. **Regular trivia is an open buzzer race, the same as ALL PLAY.** Half the wheel hands the spinning team's turn to whoever buzzes fastest.
3. **The TV goes blank at Game Over.** A CSS bug hides the end screen, and the Double Down banner never shows either.
4. **There is no Final Chaos round.** The game just stops after the last Next Turn.

There is also no text input on phones, no countdown timer and no sound.

Pacing: the game picks 3 rounds for 4–8 teams. My model's estimates are 12 turns, about 24 minutes of play, for 4 teams, and about 47 minutes for 8. That is half the 60–75 minute target, and each team spins only 3 times.

Balance: what the spinning team can expect to win ranges from about 10–21 points (trivia, which someone else usually wins) to 150 (a dare). That is a 15x spread decided by the wheel.

Runaway leader: suppose one team (say the teenagers) wins buzz races 3x as often as each other team. Under the current rules that team wins 51% of 4-team games (fair share 25%) and 43% of 6-team games (fair 17%). Under the proposed rules it wins 26% and 19%.

Dares come up rarely: P(no dare all game) is 11% with 4 teams, and 42% of teams never perform anything in their 3 spins.

**Verified** by driving the real server with socket.io and headless Edge: Sound It Out leak, trivia hijack, no buzzer lockout after a wrong answer, all four Double Down leaks, steal from a 0-point team creating points from nothing, a double-clicked Next Turn skipping a team, no finale, blank TV end screen, hidden Double Down banner. All minute and percentage figures are Monte Carlo estimates from my assumed answer rates; I did not measure them.

**60-second pitch for the redesign:** "Spin on your phone. Your team plays what the wheel lands on. Answer before the clock runs out, or the other teams can steal. Some spins pick ONE of you at random to perform. Everyone answers ALL PLAY on their phone. After the last round, bet your points in Final Chaos."

**Proposed wheel (12 slots):** Christmas Trivia x2, Pop Culture x1, Quick List x1, Dare x2, Showdown x1, Sound It Out x1, ALL PLAY (typed) x1, Hot Seat x1, Double Down x1, Grinch Steal x1. Set rounds to clamp(round(20/teams), 3, 6). Add the Final Chaos wager round.

Per-segment values the model expects for the spinning team under the proposed table: trivia 128 (plus 33 to stealers), Showdown 108 (plus 100 to the opponent), Sound It Out 152, Quick List 178, Dare 184, Hot Seat 195, Grinch about ±100–127, ALL PLAY about 70 to each team. The finale changes the winner in about 42–45% of games.

Files are in C:/Users/mleys/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d489c8c283eb5306/1f6a997f-d385-4b62-994e-3617bc11ff4c/scratchpad/review/game-design/:
- test.js: flow test that forks server.js on port 3863 with preload.js
- test2.js: TV visibility test
- sim.js: current-rules model
- sim2.js: current vs proposed model
- screenshots: tv-sounditout.png, phone-active-teammate-sounditout.png, tv-gameend-settled.png

The test server was killed and port 3863 is free.

findings.title: The team that has to guess the song sees its title on the TV and on their own phones
findings.detail: tv.html:442-445 always shows #sound-title = `songTitle — artist` on the TV. player.html:481-483 shows `Hum or whistle: "<title>"` to EVERY phone where isMyTurn is true, which includes the teammates who are supposed to guess. Verified: TV #sound-title visible with "O Christmas Tree — Traditional"; a Grinches teammate's phone shows the title. Other teams are told "Listen carefully and guess the song!" but get no buzzer (buzzer visible = false), so they have nothing to do either. Result: 100 free points with no tension on 1 of 12 wheel slots. Screenshots: tv-sounditout.png, phone-active-teammate-sounditout.png.
findings.fix: Pick a random hummer and send the secret to that phone only. In the server.js:144-148 sounditout branch: `const pool=Object.values(state.players).filter(p=>p.teamIndex===state.currentTeamIndex); const perf=pool.sort((a,b)=>(a.performed||0)-(b.performed||0))[0]` (or random among those tied for fewest); `perf.performed=(perf.performed||0)+1; state.performer={id:perf.id,name:perf.name}; io.to(perf.id).emit('secret',{text:`Hum: "${q.songTitle}" — ${q.artist}`});`. In publicState, redact currentChallenge (drop songTitle/answer) until answerRevealed. In tv.html, remove the sound-title block at 444-445 and show it only after reveal; show "🎵 Grandma Carol is humming — Elves, guess it!" with a 30 s timer instead. In player.html:481-483, use the 'secret' event instead of isMyTurn. When the timer runs out, open the buzzer to the other teams to steal 100 points.

findings.title: Regular trivia is an open buzzer race, identical to ALL PLAY, so the spinning team rarely wins its own question
findings.detail: server.js:130-136 handles 'trivia' and 'allplay' in one branch, and both set buzzerOpen=true for every phone. The only differences are 100 vs 150 points and the category. Verified: on Elves' trivia turn, Reindeer's Bob buzzed and won. ALL PLAY state was identical ({buzzerOpen:true}). There is no lockout either: after a wrong answer the host clicks Open Buzzer (server.js:295-299 resets buzzerWinner), and the SAME team buzzed again. The buzzer opens the instant the question appears (server.js:134), so the fastest reader wins. Model (sim.js, estimate): a trivia spin is worth only 21/17/14/10 points to the team that spun it (4/5/6/8 teams), versus 62–73 to everyone else. 6 of 12 slots behave this way, so half of "your turn" belongs to someone else.
findings.fix: Trivia: on the spin result, set `state.buzzerOpen=false; state.answeringTeam=state.currentTeamIndex; state.lockedTeams=[]`, then start a 15 s timer. Give the host ✓ Correct / ✗ Wrong buttons. On ✓, award the full value to the active team. On ✗ or timeout, `state.lockedTeams.push(currentTeamIndex); state.buzzerOpen=true` with a 3 s 'read' delay, and steals are worth half. In buzzer-press, reject `state.lockedTeams.includes(player.teamIndex)`; when the host marks a steal wrong, push that team and reopen. Player: show the buzzer only if `buzzerOpen && !lockedTeams.includes(myTeamIndex)`. ALL PLAY becomes simultaneous typed answers from every team (see the text-answer finding), so the two segments are genuinely different.

findings.title: The TV shows a blank screen at Game Over, and the Double Down banner never appears
findings.detail: tv.html:180-181 sets `#end-screen { display:none }`. The JS show()/hide() helpers (397-398, 522, 574) only toggle the `.hidden` class, so the ID rule keeps the screen hidden. Verified with headless Edge after game-end: #end-screen computed display = none, and the TV main area is empty. The header still reads "Round 4 of 4 / Reindeer's turn" (tv-gameend-settled.png). The same mismatch hides #double-down-banner (tv.html:199-200 display:none; the JS at 503-505 toggles .hidden instead of .show). Verified: computed display = none while doubleDownActive=true. The climax of the night happens on phones only.
findings.fix: tv.html:181: change `display: none;` to `display: flex;` and give the markup at line 290 `class="hidden"`. tv.html:200: delete `display: none;` and the `.show` rule at line 211 (the markup at 276 already starts with class="hidden"). In the game-end handler (573), also set round-label to 'Final Results' and clear turn-banner. Later, replace the instant list with a reverse-order podium reveal (see the finale finding).

findings.title: There is no Final Chaos round: the game ends abruptly after the last Next Turn
findings.detail: server.js:309-318: when round > totalRounds, phase becomes 'gameend' immediately and the sorted list is emitted. There is no wager, no final question, no typed answers, no dramatic reveal and no tiebreak. Verified: game-end fires straight from the last next-turn. Model (sim.js): the leader going into the last round wins 42–62% of games and the last-place team wins 1–5%, so trailing teams have nothing to play for at the end.
findings.fix: Add phases: 'final-intro' (TV: "FINAL CHAOS" plus the category, e.g. 'Christmas Movies'). Then 'final-wager': each team submits 0..max(score,300) on a phone, 30 s; "Santa's loan" means every team has something at stake; one wager per team, last submit wins. Then 'final-question': TV shows the question with a 45 s countdown and music, and each team types an answer. Then 'final-reveal': the host taps Next per team, ordered from lowest to highest score; TV shows the team's typed answer → ✓/✗ sound → wager → score counts up/down. Finally 'gameend' with a podium revealed 3rd → 2nd → 1st plus a fanfare. Tie → 'Sudden Death: closest number' typed question. Optionally freeze the TV scoreboard during the last regular round and reveal it just before the wager. Model (sim2.js): the finale changes the winner in about 42–45% of games. If that is too swingy, cap wagers at max(score/2, 300).

findings.title: No typed answers anywhere, despite the user asking for 'buzzer or type answers'
findings.detail: The only text inputs are the player name (player.html:255) and host fields. Verified: 0 input/textarea elements in the phone's #game-screen. In addition, every phone receives the answer: publicState sends the whole currentChallenge (verified: a Reindeer phone's state contained answer 'Scrooged'). Anyone curious can read it with dev tools, which matters more once typed answers are scored.
findings.fix: Add a generic typed-answer phase: `state.answerWindow={mode:'allplay'|'final'|'tiebreak', deadline, submissions:{[teamIndex]:{text,by}}}`. Phone: a textbox plus Submit, editable until the deadline; one answer per team, last teammate's submission wins; teammates see "Ann submitted ✓". Server auto-marks with normalize() (lowercase, strip punctuation and leading 'the/a', Levenshtein ≤2 for answers longer than 5 characters) plus an optional `accept:[]` array in questions.json. The host sees every answer with ✓/✗ toggles to override, and the TV reveals answers team by team. Redact `answer`/`songTitle` from publicState until reveal; the host gets them via `io.to(hostSocket)` or a separate 'host-state' event.

findings.title: Default length is roughly half the 60–75 minute target, and each team gets only 3 spins
findings.detail: recommendedRounds (server.js:59-63) returns 3 for every count from 4 to 8 teams (lines 61-62 are the same branch twice). Model (sim.js, about 2 min/turn including spin, reading, banter; estimate): 4 teams = 12 turns ≈ 24 min of play (about 29 with setup), 5 = 15 turns ≈ 30, 6 = 18 ≈ 36, 8 = 24 ≈ 47. With no timers, turn length depends entirely on the host. A 60–75 min party needs about 20 turns, a ~9 min finale and ~5 min setup.
findings.fix: `function recommendedRounds(n){ return Math.max(3, Math.min(6, Math.round(20 / n))); }` gives 2–3 teams: 6, 4: 5, 5: 4, 6–8: 3. Show an estimate in the host lobby (`≈ ${Math.round(5 + teams*rounds*2.6 + 9)} min`). Add timers (see the timer finding) so turns stay at about 2.5 min. Model (sim2.js) with the proposed rules: 4 teams ≈ 58 min, 6 ≈ 54 min, 8 ≈ 67 min, finale included. For 9+ teams use 2 rounds.

findings.title: Non-active teams wait 10–14 minutes between turns with nothing to do on most spins
findings.detail: With about 2 min/turn, a team waits ~5 turns (≈10 min) between its spins with 6 teams, and ~14 min with 8. Their phones only do something on trivia/ALL PLAY (6/12 slots), and that engagement comes from hijacking the active team's turn. During Dare, Sound It Out, Hot Seat, Steal and Double Down (the other 6/12) the phone just says "X's turn" (player.html:451-453). Six dares already say the audience votes (dare-009, 011, 013, 014, 015, 016), but there is no way to vote.
findings.fix: Layer cheap hooks: (a) steal-on-miss for trivia and Sound It Out at half value (see trivia finding). (b) Other teams vote 👍/👎 on their phones for performance dares: 'vote-open' with a 15 s deadline, a live applause meter on TV, majority = Nailed it 200, otherwise Good try 100. (c) Grinch Steal and Showdown pull specific rival teams into the action. (d) A 'Round Break' between rounds: one typed ALL PLAY question for every team (100 points, 20 s), so every phone has something to do every ~8–12 minutes even with 8 teams.

findings.title: Buzzer speed decides the game: one fast-thumbed team wins about half of all games
findings.detail: 50% of spins are open buzz races worth 100–150 points, with no lockout and no read delay (server.js:130-136, 242-255, 295-299). Model (sim2.js, estimate): if one team wins buzz races 3x as often as each other team, it wins 51% of 4-team games (fair 25%), 43% of 6-team (fair 17%) and 37% of 8-team (fair 13%). There is no comeback mechanic: the steal target is whoever the host chooses, and there is no finale. Mixed-age families are hit hardest: phone-native teens beat grandparents on reaction time, not knowledge.
findings.fix: Active team answers first, with steals at half value and lockout (trivia finding). Typed simultaneous ALL PLAY where only a +50 bonus goes to the first correct answer. A 3 s read delay before any buzzer opens. Grinch Steal only from teams ahead of you, and a 1st-place team must gift 100 to last place. Final wager with a 300 minimum. Model with these rules: the fast team wins 26% / 19% / 14% (4/6/8 teams), close to its fair share.

findings.title: Points per wheel slot vary 15x for the spinning team, so the wheel, not the players, decides each turn
findings.detail: Current table: trivia 100, Pop 100, Dare 150, Sound It Out 100, ALL PLAY 150, Hot Seat 25 x 5, Steal 100, Double Down 0 (server.js:18-31). Model (sim.js) of what the spinning team gets per slot: trivia 10–21, ALL PLAY 15–31 (both mostly go to other teams), Hot Seat 90, Steal +100 (and −90 to a rival), Sound It Out 105 (inflated by the leak), Dare 150. With 3 spins per team, P(a team never lands a dare) = 58%.
findings.fix: Adopt the recommended point table (separate finding). It narrows the spinning team's expected points to about 100–200 per slot (sim2.js): trivia 128 (+33 to stealers), Showdown 108 (+100 opponent), Sound It Out 152, Quick List 178, Dare 184, Hot Seat 195, Grinch about ±100–127, ALL PLAY ~70 to each team. Adding a choice (difficulty) lets skill and nerve matter.

findings.title: Too few silly physical challenges: dares are only 2 of 12 slots
findings.detail: The user's brief was trivia plus silly/embarrassing physical challenges. Dare Card is 2/12 slots and Sound It Out 1/12. In a 4-team, 12-spin game: about 2.0 dares expected, P(zero dares all game) = 11.2%, and P(a given team never performs a dare or Sound It Out in its 3 spins) = 42%. Dares say 'one team member', so the team picks its usual extrovert; the shy relatives never perform.
findings.fix: Make performance 4/12 slots (Dare x2, Showdown x1, Sound It Out x1) plus a timed Hot Seat. With the longer game (about 20 spins) that is ~6–7 performance moments. The server picks a random performer each time, weighted toward players who have performed least: TV shows "🎯 It's… GRANDMA CAROL!" with a drumroll, and only that phone says "YOU'RE UP" plus any secret.

findings.title: Double Down leaks to opponents, lasts beyond the turn, doubles penalties, and only doubles the first Hot Seat answer
findings.detail: server.js:160 sets a global flag; award-points (server.js:268) doubles the NEXT award to ANY team and then clears it. Verified: (1) Elves spun Double Down then trivia; Reindeer buzzed and got 200 for a 100-point question. (2) Snowmen's Double Down respin landed on Steal; steal-execute (273-278) did not use it up, it was still active on the next team's turn, and Grinches got 200 for +100 on Sound It Out. (3) A −50 under Double Down applied −100 and used up the bonus. (4) Hot Seat 5/5 earned 150, not 250. The TV text (tv.html:456 'Next correct answer or completed dare') does not match.
findings.fix: server.js:160: `state.doubleDown={teamIndex:state.currentTeamIndex}`. Award (268): `if(state.doubleDown && teamIndex===state.doubleDown.teamIndex && pts>0) pts*=2;` and do NOT clear it there. Clear it in next-turn (after line 306). publicState sends doubleDown. Banner: "💫 ELVES' POINTS ARE DOUBLED THIS TURN!" Hot Seat then doubles every correct answer naturally.

findings.title: Steal: the host picks the target, it can create points from nothing, and it can be clicked repeatedly
findings.detail: The host chooses the target (host.html:575-590; the phone says 'The host will pick a team…', player.html:495), so the best social moment, the spinning team choosing a victim, is taken from the players. server.js:273-278 floors the victim at 0 but always adds 100. Verified: stealing from a 0-point team gave Snowmen +100 while the victim stayed at 0. A second click applied again (Snowmen 200). There is no guard against one-sided dog-piling or the leader stealing more.
findings.fix: Rename it 'GRINCH!'. The spinning team picks on their phone: a 'steal-pick' event accepted only from the active team's sockets, with targets limited to teams with more points. Amount = Math.min(150, target.score). If the spinning team is in 1st, they must give 100 to last place ('the Grinch's heart grew'). After it runs, set state.phase='resolved' and reject further steals. TV: target's score flashes red, coins slide across, plus a sound.

findings.title: No countdown timer anywhere, though every dare has a time limit in the data
findings.detail: Every dare in dares.json has `time` (20–90 s) but no client reads it (grep finds no `.time` usage in public/ or server.js). Trivia, Hot Seat and Sound It Out are untimed, so there is no tension and turns can run as long as the host lets them.
findings.fix: Server: `state.timer={endsAt:Date.now()+ms,label}` plus `serverNow` in every state-update (clients compute an offset to avoid phone clock skew); emit 'timer-end' with setTimeout. Host: a 'Start timer' button, defaulting to the dare's `time` or 15 s trivia / 30 s Sound It Out / 40 s Hot Seat. TV: a big ring countdown that turns red with beeps in the last 5 s. Phones: the same small countdown. On timer-end, auto-close typed answers and open steals.

findings.title: No sound at all: spin, landing, buzz, right/wrong, timer and winner are silent
findings.detail: No Audio, AudioContext, <audio> or vibrate anywhere in public/*.html. Game-show energy comes largely from audio cues (ticking wheel, buzzer honk, ding/wah-wah, drumroll, fanfare).
findings.fix: TV-only WebAudio synth effects (no asset files, about 60 lines): a tick each time a segment passes the pointer (in tv.html spinToTarget's frame loop, when Math.floor(deg/segDeg) changes), landing 'ta-da', buzz-in honk, correct ding-ding when the host awards positive points, wah-wah on negative, last-5-second beeps, drumroll plus fanfare at the finale. Add a one-time 'Click to start the show 🔊' overlay on the TV to satisfy browser autoplay rules.

findings.title: Landing, scoring and round changes are visually flat; the wheel is too small to read from the sofa
findings.detail: Landing: spinToTarget is called with onDone=null (tv.html:540), and the spin-result handler is empty (543-545), so there is no slice highlight or rule card; plain text appears 0.5 s later. Scoring: renderScoreboard (402-411) just replaces innerHTML: no '+200', no count-up, not sorted by rank (only the end screens sort), no leader crown. Rounds and turns only change header text (565-571). Wheel: 380 px (line 271) with 5.5-unit labels in a 220-unit viewBox, roughly 9–10 px text on a 1080p TV (tv-sounditout.png).
findings.fix: During a spin, enlarge the wheel to about 80vh with a dimmed background. On landing, flash the slice for 1 s, then show a 3 s rule card from a new `rule` field on each WHEEL_SEGMENTS entry ("DARE — a random player performs. 200 / 100 / 0"). Sort the scoreboard by score with a FLIP reorder animation, a floating '+200' on the team row, and 👑 on the leader. Full-screen interstitials: 'ROUND 2 OF 5', and 'ELVES — YOU'RE UP!' when a turn starts.

findings.title: Many dares' scoring rules can't be applied with the host's buttons; some spoil themselves or need another team
findings.detail: Host buttons are only +base, +50, −50, −100 (host.html:563-569). Dares require −25 (dare-005, 024), −10 per wrong (017), +20 per line (018), +25 per 10 'Ho's (023), half points = 75 (025), and 'audience scores 1–5. 30+ points = full' (014). Several compare teams when only one team plays: 'Fastest team… wins the bonus' (003), 'Most stacked wins' (007), 'First person on the team' (008), 'funniest pose (voted by other teams) wins the full 150' (015). dare-022 'Silent Night... Miming' names the song the teammates must guess, and the TV shows it (verified: it was drawn, and tv.html:437 renders title and description). dare-010/012/020 need a secret that the host must whisper.
findings.fix: Standardize every dare to Nailed it 200 / Good try 100 / Refused 0 (host buttons to match) and delete point arithmetic from the descriptions. Move the comparison dares (003, 007, 008, 015, 023) into the new Showdown segment. Add a `secret` field (010 movie, 012 reindeer, 020 gift, 022 song) delivered only to the performer's phone, and retitle 022 'Mime a Carol'.

findings.title: Hot Seat is untimed and pays less than a dare
findings.detail: server.js:150-156 plus host.html:563-564: 5 untimed questions at 25 points each, max 125 (model average 90), versus 150 for a dare. The host clicks +25 and Next five times, and other teams just watch for about 2.5 minutes.
findings.fix: Make it a solo clock round: the server picks one random player from the active team, who answers alone, with a 40 s timer and as many questions as fit (queue about 10). The host gets big ✓ / ✗ / Pass buttons that award and advance in one click (server increments hotSeatIndex). 50 points per correct, max 300. TV shows a giant clock and running tally, with a sound on each answer. If it turns out too generous in play, use 40 points per correct.

findings.title: The spinning team makes no decisions all game
findings.detail: The wheel is random, the host picks steal targets and dare options, and the team only presses SPIN. Decisions (risk vs. safety, who to target) are where tension and table talk come from. questions.json already has difficulty levels (Christmas 15 easy / 15 medium / 10 hard; Pop 10/9/6) that are never used.
findings.fix: Add four decisions, each a single phone tap. (1) Trivia: choose Easy 100 / Medium 200 / Hard 300 before the question is shown; use pickQuestion(category, difficulty) and fall back to the next difficulty when one runs out. (2) Grinch target. (3) Showdown opponent. (4) Final wager. Each decision needs a 10 s auto-pick so the game never stalls.

findings.title: Proposed segment and point table (12 slots plus finale)
findings.detail:
• Christmas Trivia x2 / Pop Culture x1: active team picks Easy 100 / Medium 200 / Hard 300 and answers in 15 s. On a miss, other teams steal at half (50/100/150), one try per team, no penalty.
• Quick List x1 (new): 'Name Santa's reindeer / Christmas movies / things in a stocking' in 30 s; host taps +1. 25 per item, max 250.
• Dare x2: random performer. Nailed it 200 / Good try 100 / Refused 0; audience dares decided by other teams' phone votes.
• Showdown x1 (new): active team picks an opponent; one random player each, head to head (oven-mitt wrap, candy-cane hook, Ho-Ho count). Winner 200, tie 100 each.
• Sound It Out x1: random hummer with the secret on their phone only; team guesses in 30 s for 200. On timeout, others buzz to steal 100.
• ALL PLAY x1: every team types an answer in 20 s. 100 to each correct team, +50 to the first correct.
• Hot Seat x1: one random player alone, 40 s rapid-fire, pass allowed. 50 per correct, max 300.
• Double Down x1: spin again; the active team's positive points this turn ×2, expiring at Next Turn.
• Grinch Steal x1: active team takes min(150, target score) from any team ahead of them; if 1st, gives 100 to last place.
• Round Break (between rounds, optional for 6+ teams): one typed ALL PLAY, 100.
• Final Chaos: wager 0..max(score,300), typed answer in 45 s, ±wager, reveal from lowest score to highest. Tie → closest-number typed question.
Current for comparison: trivia 100, ALL PLAY 150, Dare 150, Sound It Out 100, Hot Seat 25 x 5, Steal 100, Double Down 0.
findings.fix: Implement as WHEEL_SEGMENTS entries with new types ('list', 'showdown', 'grinch') and per-type `rule` text; new data files data/lists.json (~15 prompts) and showdown entries in dares.json (type:'showdown'). Model (sim2.js) expected points for the spinning team: trivia 128 (+33 stealers), Quick List 178, Dare 184, Showdown 108 (+100 opponent), Sound It Out 152, ALL PLAY ~70 to each team, Hot Seat 195, Grinch ±100–127. That range is about 2x, versus 15x today.

findings.title: Improvements ranked by fun per effort (S ≈ under 1 h, M ≈ 2–4 h)
findings.detail:
1. Fix the TV end-screen and Double Down banner CSS (S, 3 lines).
2. Sound It Out secret goes to one random hummer; hide the title on TV (S).
3. Trivia: active team answers first, steal-on-miss with lockout and a 3 s read delay (S/M).
4. rounds = clamp(round(20/teams), 3, 6) (S, 1 line).
5. Limit Double Down to the active team and turn (S, 6 lines).
6. Countdown timer from server endsAt, using dares' existing `time` (S/M).
7. TV sound effects via WebAudio plus an audio-unlock overlay (S/M).
8. Random performer for dares, with secrets to their phone (S, reuses #2).
9. Final Chaos wager plus typed answers plus reverse-order reveal (M; the biggest single fun gain).
10. Typed ALL PLAY and Round Break (M, shares #9's code).
11. Phone 👍/👎 voting on performance dares (M).
12. Grinch Steal chosen by the active team, capped, one-shot (S).
13. Pick-your-difficulty trivia (S, data already exists).
14. TV landing flash, rule card, ranked animated scoreboard, round splash, bigger wheel (M).
15. Timed solo Hot Seat (S).
16. Quick List segment (S plus ~15 prompts).
17. Showdown segment reusing the comparison dares (M).
18. Standardize dare scoring 200/100/0 (S, content).
19. Hint on demand, tiebreaker, rules cards (S each).
findings.fix: Do 1–8 first: about one evening of work, and they fix every critical issue. Then 9–11 deliver the user's explicit asks (typed answers, a finale, engaged idle teams). Items 12–19 are polish and variety.

findings.title: The hint appears automatically on TV with every question, making questions too easy
findings.detail: tv.html:461-463 appends 'Hint: …' to every trivia question. Verified on screen: 'What 1988 Christmas movie stars Bill Murray… | Hint: It's a modern retelling of A Christmas Carol'. With buzzers open, this rewards fast readers even more and makes every question feel equally easy.
findings.fix: Hide hints by default. Add a host 'Give hint' button (emits 'hint-revealed'), or let the active team 'buy a hint' on their phone for half points. Sound It Out's hint stays host-only.

findings.title: Ties for 1st are common and not handled; medals are assigned arbitrarily
findings.detail: All awards are multiples of 50/100, and the model (sim.js) shows 10–14% of current games ending in a tie for 1st. The end screens (tv.html:575-578, host.html:673-677, player.html:562-570) give medals by sort position, so one tied team gets silver arbitrarily.
findings.fix: If the top scores are tied after the finale: 'SUDDEN DEATH — closest number wins'. Tied teams type a number on their phones (e.g. 'How many lights are on the Rockefeller Center tree?' ~50,000), the server picks the closest, and the TV reveals it. Show '🥇🥇' with 'TIE' if the host skips the tiebreaker.

findings.title: No rules are shown anywhere, so families can't learn the game in 60 seconds
findings.detail: grep finds no 'rules' or 'how to play' text. The TV lobby (tv.html:260-265) shows only 'Waiting for host to start the game…'. Every segment's rules live only in the host's head.
findings.fix: The TV lobby rotates a 4-line card: '1) Spin on your phone. 2) Your team plays what it lands on — beat the clock or others steal. 3) Some spins pick ONE of you to perform. 4) Bet it all in FINAL CHAOS.' Add a one-line `rule` to each WHEEL_SEGMENTS entry and show it for 3 s on landing and on phones, so players learn each segment the first time it comes up.

findings.title: Double-clicking Next Turn skips a team's turn, and nothing reminds the host to award points first
findings.detail: server.js:306-334 accepts next-turn with no guard. Verified: two quick next-turn emits went Elves → Snowmen, skipping Reindeer entirely. For a family game, a skipped turn feels unfair and is hard to undo.
findings.fix: Have the client send `{expectedTeamIndex}` and ignore the event if it doesn't match state.currentTeamIndex. Disable the host button for 1 s after a click. If no points were awarded during the turn, ask 'Next turn without awarding points?'.

findings.title: Phones give no 'it's you' moment
findings.detail: When it's your team's turn there is only a 3 s toast (player.html:603-608). During the spin the phone shows only 'Spinning…'. There is no haptic or full-screen cue.
findings.fix: Full-screen 'YOUR TURN — SPIN!' with a swipe-up-to-spin gesture (cosmetic; the server still decides the result). '👀 Look at the TV!' while spinning. Use navigator.vibrate([200,100,200]) on Android (iOS ignores it). A full-screen gold 'YOU'RE UP, CAROL!' when picked as performer, with the secret shown under a press-and-hold to reveal.
